The most likely path (EC-2: Failure Path pushes a `[skip ci]` abort commit onto a branch with an existing open PR) was completely unguarded. Outcome verification closes both the detection gap and the abuse path.

summary: #363 — dev-failure dispatch cap is owned by the router, three distinct failed SHAs per FID
description: `MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS: 3` is a workflow-level `env:` in `.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml` (and its template copy), held equal to `THRESHOLDS` in `.bkit/src/commands/workflow/counters.ts` by `counters.test.ts`. It counts distinct failed SHAs per FID, all-time, checked and written in the ctx step of both dispatch jobs before dispatch; a value that is not a whole number refuses the dispatch (fail-closed). The telemetry commit is `[skip ci]` and origin/dev presence is verified after one retry. One surface (`dev`), not two — `fix/**` was never built. `bkit_dev_dispatch_guard` is an inline copy in each job of `bkit-cloud.yml`, not a shared script.
rationale: the per-session counters (MAX_NORMAL_ATTEMPT / MAX_DEBUG_ATTEMPT) reset on every new cloud dispatch and cannot bound a cross-session loop. Writing the row before dispatch means an early /bkit-debug crash cannot undercount; fail-closed verification stops the cap degrading silently to unbounded. feat/** is pre-merge and PR-scoped, already bounded in-session. The value lives in the workflow file because its guards run before bkit is installed.
alternatives: let /bkit-debug count its own dispatches (cannot see prior sessions); cap by row count rather than distinct SHAs (double-counts retries of one SHA); cap feat/** on the same budget (already bounded in-session)

summary: #384 — ship gate requires the CI capstone green at the exact head; skipped-lane refusal is opt-in
description: `bkit runs gate --head=<sha>` (`.bkit/src/commands/workflow/runs.ts`) refuses unless the capstone job (`package.json` `bkit.capstoneJob`, default `bkit-tests-check`, `if: !cancelled()`) concluded success at that head; exit 14 = stale green at a superseded head. Exit 16 (skipped lane) fires only for lanes named in `package.json` `bkit.shipGateRequiredLanes` or `--required-lanes`; the default empty list reports a skipped lane and proceeds. `ci.yml` anchors: `cancel-in-progress`, `[force full]`, `run_level=full`, `bkit-tests-check` (grep, not line numbers).
rationale: A blanket skipped-lane refusal could never pass for the CI bkit ships: an event-scoped lane (e.g. `@live` on push to dev) cannot run before merge, so the gate would refuse every PR. Required lanes are the consumer's call.
alternatives: Discarded and named here so they are not re-litigated: (1) GitHub merge queue (rebase onto base, CI on merge_group, server-side merge if green) — unavailable: bkit consumers are private + non-Enterprise, would require a merge_group trigger in every consumer ci.yml (deferral 384-merge-queue-unavailable-private-non-enterprise). (2) Required status checks on dev (extending `bkit setup protect-main` to dev) closing the UI hand-merge path — separable additive cross-consumer policy with its own plan-tier question (protection on private repos is plan-gated); deferred to 384-required-status-checks-on-dev-via-bkit-protect-main. (3) Step-1 push-capability probe (git push --dry-run) to classify Path A/B by whether the branch is pushable — rejected with mechanism: sends no ref-update, branch protection is never evaluated, false-positive strands a cloud session on a dev checkout. (4) Head-move observer as primary classifier — rejected: mis-reads a failed gh pr update-branch as unchanged and merges a stale base.

summary: Ship lands docs, summaries, ledgers and skill removals on the PR before the merge, and the merge gate carries CI forward from the last tested commit past bookkeeping-only commits
description: bkit-ship.md runs Deferred Sweep (Step 5), Update Docs & Summary (Step 6), Prune Skills (Step 7) and Commit + Push Bookkeeping (Step 8: one `bkit ledgers commit --scope=pr` `[skip ci]` commit, plain push to {SHIP_BRANCH}) before Re-validate (Step 9) and the merge. Re-validate resolves VALIDATED_HEAD = the head before that commit while the PR head is it plus bookkeeping only (`bkit ledgers only-bookkeeping`) and dev requires no status checks; `bkit runs gate --validated=` checks CI there (exit 17 otherwise). Close Workflow records a `ship-merge-ci` verdict row (`bkit status row`) and, without dev pushes, publishes its commit from a close worktree off origin/dev, falling back to a `ship-close/{FID}` PR.
rationale: The post-merge close commit had no publish channel on a cloud runtime (dev not pushable, --delete-branch removes the feature branch), which lost #380 SHIPPED row, and its pathspec never covered docs/*.md on any runtime. Carrying CI forward means a PR that arrives green spends no extra CI run on ship own docs commit.
alternatives: Keep the post-merge flush and publish it via dev push or a close PR only (smaller, but a crash between merge and close still loses docs); re-run CI after the bookkeeping push (one extra full CI run on every Path A ship).

summary: Template offers a release-PR mirror mode: a same-repo dev → default-branch PR skips its lanes and its capstone copies the dev push run's verdict
description: Adopted from a consumer. bkit-tests-scope sets mirror_push_run (run_level=none, every lane off) for a same-repo PR from dev into the default branch; bkit-tests-check runs `bkit runs mirror --head=<PR head> --branch=dev`, which polls `bkit runs gate --event=push` at the PR head and passes only on a green push-run capstone. Opt-in reference in the template scaffold, with three stated preconditions: dev pushes run full, push runs diff against the last green push run, and promotion hangs off the default-branch push run.
rationale: The release PR head is the dev tip the push run already tests, so a full PR run repeats the slowest run in the repo. Reusing the ship gate keeps one run-selection and capstone-lookup implementation; --event push stops the PR's own run at the same SHA from counting or masking a red push run. A real, non-skipped required check is kept because a skipped required check can read as passed while the push run is red. The default-branch push run still re-runs full and gates promotion, so the mirror only gates the merge.
alternatives: Skip the release PR's required check outright — rejected: a skipped required check can pass the PR while the push run is red
Rely on the existing Check SHA Cache step — rejected: it only short-circuits after the push run finished green; an in-flight or red push run still triggers a full duplicate
Inline poll loop in the workflow YAML — rejected: the required check's logic must be unit-tested code
New standalone run-lookup implementation — rejected: duplicates `bkit runs gate` run selection and capstone lookup

summary: #341 OQ-A confirmed, OQ-D withdrawn: design/plan close lands via a local squash + dev push when the runtime can push dev, else via a {BRANCH}->dev PR merged with gh (D5(a), not push_files); the landed subject keeps `bkit [skip ci]`, so a docs-only close dispatches no CI
description: Design and plan Close Workflow branch on RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES (from the `runtime-resolved` row). true: under the dev lock, `git merge --squash -X ours feat/{FID}` on a dev checkout, `bkit roadmap feature`, one path-scoped `docs({FID}): <phase> DONE bkit [skip ci]` commit via `bkit ledgers commit --squash-of=feat/{FID}`, `bkit branches push --mode=dev`, then worktree and branch cleanup. false (e.g. a claude.ai cloud session): commit the roadmap update, push {BRANCH} (`bkit branches push --mode=feature`), open or reuse the {BRANCH}->dev PR titled `docs({FID}): <phase> DONE` (`bkit prs open --existing=reuse`), and merge it with `gh pr merge --squash --subject "docs({FID}): <phase> DONE bkit [skip ci]" --body ""` (mapped MCP `merge_pull_request` when RUNTIME_GITHUBCLI=false); the landed SHA is the PR's merge commit (`bkit prs probe`). Both paths then run `bkit prs scan-body` over the landed commit BODY (subject excluded) and `bkit prs cross-check`, and append a `close-transport` row with `bkit prs transport-row --kind=close`. The merge does not wait for CI: the landed subject carries `bkit [skip ci]`, so a docs-only close dispatches no run. The OQ-D CI-cost reversal accepted at build (drop `[skip ci]` from every phase-close and intermediate status subject) is withdrawn.
rationale: Spike B (closed, folded into the design) found push_files (D5) cannot express `merge --squash -X ours`, inlines full file content per call (non-repairable payload bloat), and inverts conflict semantics (branch-wins vs dev-wins) -- three defects that demote it from primary. D5(a) is uniform with ship's server-side merge and avoids the push_files payload/conflict/credential-coupling defects. OQ-D was reversed: a deliberate `bkit [skip ci]` on a docs-only SUBJECT is the CI-minutes convention, and stripping it also breaks ship's promotion-lag guard in `bkit branches switch`, which stops a ship (exit 82) when a local dev commit ahead of origin/dev lacks the token. The real defect is a token inherited into a squash BODY; every close passes an explicit --body "" and `bkit prs scan-body` scans the landed BODY only. bkit-skip-ci-subject-audit.test.ts asserts both halves.
alternatives: D5 (push_files) as shape-A primary -- REJECTED per Spike B (non-repairable payload bloat, conflict-semantics inversion, credential coupling shared with gh's own flaky mode-3 auth). Dropping `[skip ci]` from every phase-close and intermediate status subject (the original OQ-D) -- REJECTED on reversal: one full dev CI run per docs-only close and a broken ship promotion-lag guard; the inherited-token risk is met by an explicit empty squash body plus a landed-body scan.

summary: pnpm + package.json required in every consumer repo as bkit tooling; consumer stack stays free behind bkit:gate:* scripts
description: Every consumer repo needs Node, a `package.json` and pnpm. They are bkit tooling, like `git`, `gh` and `jq`. The consumer stack (language, framework, database, host) stays free: gates are `bkit:gate:*` scripts that wrap any command, e.g. a Python repo declares `"bkit:gate:static-unit": "ruff check && pytest"` in a stub `package.json`. Commands that run the consumer package manager build the call in one module, `.bkit/src/commands/shared/package-manager.ts` (`PACKAGE_RUNNER`); no other command spells `pnpm` literally, so reversing this decision is a one-file change for the workflow commands. A gate that cannot run (exit 126/127) makes `bkit tests run` exit 4, which routes to the Failure Path, never `TEST_VERDICT=FAIL`.
rationale: bkit installs and upgrades itself with pnpm: `bkit upgrade --latest` shells out to `pnpm view` / `pnpm add` (`.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts`), and cloud setup plus GitHub Packages auth (DE-31) are pnpm-specific. Installing bkit as a devDependency with pnpm makes the consumer repo a pnpm repo, so "bkit uses pnpm, project uses npm" is not a real option: the choice is pnpm everywhere or no pnpm assumption anywhere (about 10 source files). Both consumers already use pnpm. Cost: a JS team on npm / yarn / bun must switch to pnpm to adopt bkit; revisit when one appears.
alternatives: Package-manager agnostic everywhere (detect from lockfile; `bkit branches rebase` already keys lockfile regeneration on the lockfile name for 7 ecosystems via `LOCKFILE_REGENERATE`): rejected for now, needs bkit install / upgrade / cloud setup / auth docs reworked with no consumer needing it. Agnostic gate runner only, pnpm for bkit itself: rejected, incoherent because installing bkit with pnpm already makes the repo a pnpm repo.

summary: .bkit/issues.jsonl is the canonical feature ledger; docs/roadmap.md is its regenerated projection
description:
Design Addendum 3 § N-O (owner, 2026-07-27) inverted the authority model a second time: .bkit/issues.jsonl (kind: "feature", append-only, six-state status ladder) is canonical, appended at every phase close; docs/roadmap.md is fully regenerated from it on every fold, never upserted.
- **Current (checked 2026-10-09):** The ledger is `.bkit/issues.jsonl` (`kind:"feature"`). `bkit roadmap fold` (`.bkit/src/commands/workflow/roadmap.ts`) reads it as the sole input; every phase close appends its row and re-renders through `bkit roadmap feature`. Shape unchanged: append-only JSONL is canonical, `docs/roadmap.md` is a full regenerate.
rationale: A full-regenerate projection over an append-only merge=union ledger is reproducible from scratch and sidesteps the per-FID upsert + KN-42 duplicate-collapse invariant entirely.
alternatives: Per-FID upsert on docs/roadmap.md as canonical (Directive 1, design Addendum 1) — REJECTED: build/debug rows on feat/{FID} are not re-derivable from dev, so a blind regenerate would revert them; the ledger removes the need for upsert semantics altogether.

summary: Two consumer Notes blocks on the board, never overwritten
description: `docs/roadmap.md` carries two `bkit:roadmap-notes-{pre,post}` marker pairs. `bkit roadmap fold` re-emits each body unchanged and seeds a placeholder for a missing pair; `notes-post` is last and absorbs any consumer text after the final marker. Region order: notes-pre / roadmap-status / roadmap-analysis / notes-post. There is no `notes-mid` — it sat between the bkit and tracker lists, and the tracker list is gone.
rationale: Users need durable free-form notes next to the generated lists. Head and Backlog cannot sit between those lists, and rewriting the whole generated region would wipe anything written there.
alternatives: Preserve unnamed gaps between generated marker pairs — REJECTED: the fold rewrites the region in full so a new mechanical block can be introduced without a migration, and unnamed gaps have no owner. Sidecar notes file — REJECTED: notes belong next to the lists they annotate.

summary: step-skipped is an additive status.jsonl audit row the fold reducer ignores, not a folded event
description: A skipped conditional step appends {type:"step-skipped", workflow, step, reason, decidedBy, at, parentSha} to status.jsonl. The reducer's fallthrough arm ignores it, so it never enters WorkflowRun.steps and is absent from the StatusEvent union in bkit-status.ts — the same treatment runtime-resolved, transport-fallback and close-transport already get. decidedBy is a closed enum: caller-flag | upstream-verdict | applicability | path-override. reason names the absent input, never a size judgement.
rationale: `bkit counters derive --position=count` and `--position=current` derive attempt numbers from the folded run's steps array, which only step-done populates. Folding step-skipped would make a deliberate skip indistinguishable from an attempt and mis-terminate every attempt-bounded loop in build and debug. Keeping it out of the fold also keeps it union-merge safe: duplicate rows are inert because nothing reduces them.
alternatives: fold it as a Step with status:"SKIPPED" (breaks attempt counters); add a skipped:true field to a step-done row (a skipped step has no verdict, artifacts or attempt to report, and readers filtering on step-done would count it as executed); write nothing and derive skips from absence (the status quo, which cannot distinguish a skip from a crash)

summary: The board carries two Notes blocks, not three, and renders no tracker table
description: `bkit roadmap fold` rewrites the whole generated region in one pass: Notes (notes-pre) / roadmap-status / roadmap-analysis / Notes (notes-post). There is no roadmap-notes-mid pair and no tracker block. Consumer text above the first marker is preserved byte-for-byte; text after the last marker is carried into notes-post so that block stays last.
rationale: notes-mid existed only to give the consumer somewhere to write between the bkit list and the tracker list. With no tracker list it has nothing to sit between.

summary: There is no tracker snapshot: bkit copies no tracker data into the repo and has no kind:"tracker" row shape
description: bkit copies the tracker nowhere: no sync step, no snapshot file, no tracker marker block on the board, no tracker row shape in `.bkit/jsonl.md`.
rationale: docs/roadmap.md renders only what has no other home. A wired tracker already shows its own issues and its own closures, so a regenerated copy is a second source that can only go stale. Open tracker issues reach the board through the analysis block as ranked recommendations, never as a mechanical table.

summary: No close reads the tracker, because nothing on the board comes from the tracker
description: No phase close reads the tracker, runs a drift check, or evaluates a cadence. Every phase close does one thing: `bkit roadmap feature` appends its feature row to `.bkit/issues.jsonl` and re-renders the roadmap-status block from the ledger (fail-open, never gates the close).
rationale: The question of whether a close should enrich from the tracker disappears once the board holds no tracker-derived rows to enrich.

summary: Consumer text on the board is preserved verbatim and never special-cased; there is no Backlog strip
description: notes-post is last. A `## Backlog / Ideas` heading in a consumer's board is carried into notes-post like any other consumer text; `bkit roadmap fold` recognises and drops no heading.
rationale: The Backlog seed only ever shipped on dev, so no consumer has one to migrate. A fold that recognises and deletes a specific heading is a rule that can only fire on text bkit itself wrote, and preserving every byte is the simpler contract.

summary: No shortlist agent: the roadmap analysis reads open bkit FIDs' plan artifacts in full and the tracker as titles and links, with descriptions only for the next milestone, the next umbrella and their relevant children
description: @bkit-roadmap-shortlist is deleted. @bkit-utility-update-roadmap refreshes docs/roadmap.md with `bkit roadmap fold` and treats the human Notes blocks as pointers, never instructions. Per FID in Design / Plan / Build / Debug in the bkit block it reads the matching docs/plans/** design and plan artifacts; Shipped rows are skipped. It folds open deferrals and failures. With a tracker wired it reads OPEN issue titles and links only, never comments, then picks the next milestone and the next umbrella and reads descriptions only for those two containers and their relevant children (open, unblocked, startable now).
rationale: The token measurement that forced two passes still holds — comments are 78% of the content — so comments are never read. No recorded rationale exists for moving the choice of which tracker issues get a description read from the Notes author to the agent.

summary: #384 ship-bookkeeping lands AFTER #341 (d64ef5be merged); 384 re-derives against the post-#341 bkit-ship.md — outcome: 341-first-landed
description: Pre-flight gate for #384 (ship bookkeeping mutates validated PR head). #341 (CLOSED, merged d64ef5be) landed the post-#341 ship markers first: the ship runtime-resolved row writer is present once at bkit-ship.md:320 at d64ef5be, now `bkit runtime row --workflow=ship` at .bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md:348, RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES appears 10x. #384 takes the post-#341 bkit-ship.md as its diff base: `git log --oneline d64ef5be..HEAD -- .bkit/workflows/bkit-ship.md` is empty (no intervening rewrite). No concurrent PR/branch rewrites bkit-ship.md — feat/58-workflow-counters and worktree-374-test-lane-coverage carry 0 bkit-ship.md-touching commits past origin/dev. Ship remains the documented exception: Step 13 switches with `bkit branches switch`, never `bkit prs guard-checkout`, which restores the pre-checkout branch and would undo staying on dev for Steps 14-15 (`.bkit/workflows.md:138`). Comment corrections folded into issue context by design phase: (a) non-firing pull_request on a CONFLICTING PR is general GitHub behaviour, not a bkit token quirk; (b) cancel-in-progress is a second independent justification for the frozen head; (c) Path B2 is the common case, not the escape hatch.
rationale: Two workflows rewriting bkit-ship.md on the same clone would collide. Recording 341-first-landed makes the serialisation explicit and machine-checkable: any later task asserting it can grep docs/decisions.jsonl for outcome 341-first-landed on key 384-341-serialisation.
alternatives: Land 384 against pre-#341 bkit-ship.md — REJECTED: would re-derive RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES/worktree conventions that #341 already settled. Block 384 behind an open #341 PR — REJECTED: #341 is CLOSED (d64ef5be merged).

summary: Workflow mechanics run as `bkit <noun> <verb>` commands under one contract: kebab-case flags, one JSON object on stdout, `[bkit-<noun>]` logs on stderr, fixed exit-code bands
description: Every mechanical workflow step is a `bkit <noun> <verb>` command in `.bkit/src/commands/{workflow,ci,setup}/`, listed in `commands/registry.ts`; `bkit-commands.test.ts` fails on an unlisted source file and holds every command to the contract in `commands/lib.ts`. Flags: kebab-case, `--flag=value` or `--flag value`, one name for one thing everywhere (`--workflow --step --fid --month --sub-plan --attempt --verdict --artifact`). stdout: ONE JSON object, camelCase keys matching `status.jsonl`. stderr: human log lines tagged `[bkit-<noun>]`. Exit: 0 ok / 1 the answer is no (gate failed, max attempts, lock held) / 2 usage error or missing dependency; 3-79 command-specific, listed in that verb's `--help`; 80 do it via MCP (`gh` unavailable); 81 hand the wait back to the agent turn loop; 82 needs a human. `--help` renders from the verb's own spec. Nouns are plural where a repo has many (`counters`), singular where it has one (`status`). `bkit <noun> <verb>` is tried before the older top-level commands; a noun that is also a command (`status`) routes only when the second word is one of its verbs. Workflow blocks call the main checkout's binary through the fixed `BKIT=` line; the bkit repo links itself as a dev dependency for the same path. A value a later step needs is held from the JSON by key, never re-derived; `jq` in a workflow block only picks one key out of a command's output in that block. The only file in `.bkit/scripts/` is the slop plugin `bkit-slop-type-suppression.mjs`.
rationale: Stated in the #467 commits and code: the contract is fixed once in `commands/lib.ts` so flag names, output shape and exit codes are not copied per command (8d3c3dcf); `--help` and the convention test read the same spec, so help text cannot drift from what a command accepts (`commands/lib.ts` header). Repo facts each workflow worked out by hand — repo root from any worktree, UTC month, where `status.jsonl` lives, skip-CI tokens — now have one answer (8d3c3dcf); porting surfaced hand-derived bugs, e.g. macOS reading UTC timestamps as local time, which made a live run look ten hours idle and lose its lock (8dc60537). Logic lives in commands, not workflow shell, because the host shell is not guaranteed bash and a workflow body cannot take shell positional parameters — slash-command argument substitution rewrites `$N` (`.agents/rules.md` § Project Rules › Workflow bash blocks; `.bkit/workflows.md` § Workflow Authoring Rules) — and because a workflow that runs an installed script by path breaks when the consumer renames or deletes it (`.bkit/src/bkit-template-path-refs.test.ts`). The main-checkout binary works before and without a worktree `node_modules`, since design and plan worktrees never install (`.bkit/workflows.md` § Workflow commands).
alternatives: Shell scripts in `.bkit/scripts/` that workflows source or run — rejected for the reasons in the rationale. Not written down anywhere: why one JSON object rather than shell `KEY=value` lines, and why exit codes 80-82 specifically.

summary: A file bkit stops shipping is deleted only when unchanged since bkit wrote it; an edited copy is kept with an advisory, callers are reported, and no shim is left at the old path
description: `RETIRED_OWNED_FILES` (`.bkit/src/bkit-retire.ts`) lists each retired owned path and what replaced it; append-only, never remove an entry. Install and upgrade delete a listed file when it matches its `.bkit/version` `canonicalHashes` entry and drop the hash; `bkit check` reports the pending delete as drift. A consumer-edited copy, or one with no hash on record, stays and gets an advisory naming the replacement. Every line in `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `package.json` that still names a retired path gets its own advisory. No shim script is left at a retired path. A script still called by a shipped CI file is retired only after that file stops calling it (`bkit-cloud.yml` sets `MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS` as workflow env; the template `ci.yml` mirror step runs `bkit runs mirror`). Callers bkit cannot rewrite are served by the replacement command: a verb may take one bare positional argument (`FlagSpec.positional`), so a consumer CI file that passes `slop:delta` a bare base sha keeps working on `bkit ci slop`, and install / upgrade re-point a `slop:delta` value that byte-matches the old default (`LEGACY_SLOP_DELTA_SCRIPTS`, `.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts`).
rationale: Install and upgrade overwrite what bkit owns but never delete a file bkit has dropped, so a retired script would otherwise sit in every consumer repo forever; a consumer-edited copy stays; caller lines get their own advisory because nothing else tells the consumer the call now fails (`.bkit/src/bkit-retire.ts` header). Why no forwarding shim is left at a retired path is not written down.
alternatives: Delete every listed file regardless of edits — rejected: an edited or unrecorded copy is treated as the consumer's, the same rule as `de-12-bar-131-follow-up-isconsumermodified-defaults-missing-ca`. Shim scripts at retired paths forwarding to the command — not adopted; no reason is recorded.

summary: No workflow, prompt or `.bkit/wording.md` names an installed template path; mechanics come from `bkit` commands and settings from `package.json` `bkit`
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-template-path-refs.test.ts` fails when a line in `.bkit/workflows/*.md`, `.bkit/prompts/*.md` or `.bkit/wording.md` names a template path: each `.github/workflows/` template file name, `.husky/`, `.vale`, `.lintstagedrc.json`, `slop-scan.config.json`, `.envrc`, `.bkit/scripts/`, and each `scripts/<tool>` template folder. The workflow and script names are read from `.bkit/templates/`, so a new template is covered without editing the test. Settings a command needs come from `package.json` `bkit` through one reader, `.bkit/src/commands/shared/config.ts`: `ciWorkflow` (default `ci.yml`), `capstoneJob` (default `bkit-tests-check`), `worktree.copy` (default `.env`, `.env.local`), `worktree.install` (default true), `issueTracker`, `githubProject`, `shipGateRequiredLanes` (default empty). No command hard-codes a CI workflow, check name or app folder.
rationale: Templates are the consumer's once installed: they rename, delete or rewrite them (a CI workflow, a hook, a lint config, a helper script), and a workflow step that reads or runs one by path breaks the day the consumer does (`.bkit/src/bkit-template-path-refs.test.ts` header). One settings reader gives one set of defaults (`.bkit/src/commands/shared/config.ts` header).
alternatives: A hand-maintained forbidden-path list in the test — not used: names derive from the templates folder so a new template is covered without editing the test (test header). No other alternative is recorded.

summary: Sentences shared by 5+ prompts, and header sentences workflows share with prompts, live once in `.bkit/wording.md`; a test checks every copy and `pnpm wording:sync` rewrites them in place
description: `.bkit/wording.md` holds one clause per shared sentence: canonical `text`, earlier wordings in `retired`, and a mode per surface (`required` / `where-used` / `forbidden` / `if-verdict`) for prompts, workflows and the `.agents/rules.md` managed block. `.bkit/src/bkit-wording.test.ts` fails on a missing, duplicated or forbidden clause, a near-copy (80%+ similar, not equal), a retired wording, and any sentence in 5+ prompts the file does not list; it also keeps the Rules line first, External input last, the `.agents/rules.md` group headings, and the three legs of the untrusted-input sentence. `pnpm wording:sync` (`.bkit/src/bkit-wording.ts --write`) rewrites near-copies and retired wordings in place, finding copies by similarity and each clause's retired list, so prompts carry no markers. Change a shared sentence only in `.bkit/wording.md`: edit `text`, move the old wording to `retired`, run `pnpm wording:sync`. Sentences in fewer than 5 prompts stay local.
rationale: Changing a shared sentence becomes one edit plus one command instead of up to 48 hand edits (81878ecf). The check found real drift on its first run: the Destructive git line in `bkit-ship-conflict-resolve`, and a comma for a semicolon in the Tools line of six workflows (81878ecf).
alternatives: Markers in each prompt around the shared text — not used: sync finds copies by similarity and retired wordings so no markers are added (81878ecf); why markers were unwanted is not written down. Render-time assembly of prompt headers at `bkit install` — listed as deferred in `de-36-342-universal-untrusted-input-bullet-plus-glob-scoped-g`; #467 records no reason for choosing in-place sync over it.

summary: Workflows write `status.jsonl` and `.bkit/issues.jsonl` rows only through `bkit` commands; no workflow block appends with `>>`
description: Row writers: `workflow-started` / `workflow-failed` / `workflow-done` plus close telemetry → `bkit workflows start|fail|close`; `step-done` → `bkit steps done` (captures `parentSha`, writes the row, then commits, in that order); `workflow-meta` → `bkit status meta` (`--debug-mode` / `--push-mode` / `--debug-attempt` / `--plan-source` / `--soak-entry` / `--opened-pr`); `runtime-resolved` → `bkit runtime row`; `transport-fallback` / `close-transport` → `bkit prs transport-row`; any other typed audit row the fold does not model (ship's gate refusals, CI probes, timeouts, merge CI) → `bkit status row --type=`, which refuses a folded type; `kind:"feature"` rows → `bkit roadmap feature` (appends, re-renders `docs/roadmap.md`, fail-open). Reads go through `bkit status fold|route` and `bkit counters derive|rows|run`; no counter is derived by raw jq over `status.jsonl`. `bkit workflows close` runs in the worktree before the squash in both close modes, so its rows ride the branch. Gates: `bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts` (no `>>` onto `status.jsonl` or `.bkit/issues.jsonl` in any phase workflow) and `bkit-counter-prose-audit.test.ts` (no raw-jq counter).
rationale: A raw `>>` bypasses the row shape and the fail-open contract the commands own (`bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts`). `bkit steps gate` checks the row `steps done` wrote, so a step no longer types its own row and then ticks a box saying it did; `steps done` orders parentSha capture, row and commit because the fold's de-dup key needs `parentSha` to advance per attempt (`.bkit/src/commands/workflow/steps.ts` header). Close rows written in the worktree before the squash ride the branch (045e990f).
alternatives: No rejected alternative is recorded in the #467 commits, `.bkit/workflows.md` or `docs/architecture.md`.

summary: BAR-142 §A2 — .bkitignore public contract
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** `.bkitignore` is a new public file at the consumer repo root. Syntax: `#` comment, blank-line ignore, [picomatch](https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch) glob, optional `:dotted.key` suffix for per-key exclusion. Per-key is opt-in behind `BKIT_BKITIGNORE_PER_KEY=1` env var (off by default). Once shipped, the file and its syntax are a public contract.
- **Why:** Consumers legitimately override bkit-managed files (e.g. custom ci.yml jobs, additional `.claude/settings.json` hook events). `bkit check` currently reports false-positive drift for these. `.bkitignore` gives consumers a declarative escape hatch without touching the managed file itself. Per-key is opt-in because implementation cost is high and per-file covers the majority use-cases.
- **Discarded:** (1) Make per-key the default — implementation cost likely high; opt-in via env covers the primary use case. (2) Use a custom DSL instead of gitignore-style — picomatch is well-understood, has no shell-out, and is a pure-regex library (security: no injection risk). (3) Store in `.agents/.bkitignore` — consumer-owned files belong at repo root, not in the `.agents/` subtree (which is bkit-managed).
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-142 §A2, `.bkit/src/bkit-bkitignore.ts`, `docs/deferrals.jsonl` (per-key deferred)
rationale: Consumers legitimately override bkit-managed files (e.g. custom ci.yml jobs, additional `.claude/settings.json` hook events). `bkit check` currently reports false-positive drift for these. `.bkitignore` gives consumers a declarative escape hatch without touching the managed file itself. Per-key is opt-in because implementation cost is high and per-file covers the majority use-cases.

summary: #265 — Split `--tooling` into stack-agnostic `--ci` + opt-in `--typescript`
rationale: A non-Node repo could not adopt bkit's CI gate graph + prose-lint without inheriting `tsc`/`vitest`/`slop-scan`/`husky` it has no use for. Separating the agnostic foundation from the TS toolchain lets any repo install `--claude --ci` and stay green, while Node/TS repos opt into the full toolchain with `--typescript`.
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Split the `--tooling` bundle into two composable flags. `--ci` = the stack-agnostic CI/quality foundation: the `ci.yml` **skeleton** (gate graph + capstone contract + branch-protection, with Node/TS step bodies shipped as commented examples) + Vale prose-lint config; **no `package.json` footprint**. `--typescript` = the Node/TS toolchain (`tsc`, slop-scan + `boundary/type-suppression`, prettier, husky + lint-staged) + the **wired** `ci.yml` step bodies; **implies `--ci`**. `--tooling` becomes a back-compat alias for `--ci --typescript`. Re-bucket module CONTENTS (not module IDs) to avoid dispatch/registry churn: Vale config `lint → ci`; `typecheck` + slop-scan helper scripts `core-walk → lint`. `uninstall --typescript` removes only lint + git-hooks (keeps the `--ci` foundation); `uninstall --tooling` stays symmetric (removes all three).
- **Why:** A non-Node repo could not adopt bkit's CI gate graph + prose-lint without inheriting `tsc`/`vitest`/`slop-scan`/`husky` it has no use for. Separating the agnostic foundation from the TS toolchain lets any repo install `--claude --ci` and stay green, while Node/TS repos opt into the full toolchain with `--typescript`.
- **Mechanism:** The wired `ci.yml` template is the single source of truth (bkit dogfoods it); the skeleton is **derived** by `deriveCiSkeleton`, which comments out every `# bkit:start ts-ci-steps … # bkit:end ts-ci-steps` region. `dispatchModules` sets `ctx.wiredCi = modules.has("lint")` so the `ci` module seeds wired when the TS toolchain is co-installed, skeleton otherwise. This guarantees the two `ci.yml` forms never drift.
- **Discarded — re-bucket module IDs / add bare `--lint`/`--git-hooks`:** maximises churn across the dispatch registry, resolveModules, detection, and the entire test suite for no user-facing gain (lint + git-hooks always travel together under `--typescript`/`--tooling`). Kept `lint`/`git-hooks` internal-only.
- **Discarded — maintain two hand-edited `ci.yml` templates:** guaranteed drift. The derive-from-wired transform keeps one source of truth.
- **Discarded — move the `lint:prose` npm script to `--ci`:** it is a `package.json`/Node convenience and `--ci` must stay package.json-free; only the Vale **config** (stack-agnostic) ships with `--ci`. `--typescript` always co-installs `--ci`, so a TS consumer still gets the config its `lint:prose` references.
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** #265, #263 (type-suppression rule prerequisite), DE-29 (#252 CLI surface redesign), `.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts` (`deriveCiSkeleton`, `runCiModule`, `runLintModule`), `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/ci.yml`

summary: #252/#253 — v4 CLI surface: `bkit install` requires at least one module flag
description: (1) `bkit install` with no module flag exits 1 (`.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts:1325`). (2) Module flags: `--claude`, `--cursor`, `--codex`, `--opencode=<provider>`, `--typescript` (`.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts:237`); `--auto=<variant>` is the opt-in cloud module. Not flags: `--full`, `--core`, `--lint`, `--git-hooks`, `--renovate`, `--dependabot`, `--cloud`, `--dependency=`, `--ci`, `--tooling` — each exits 1 with the generic `Unknown flag` error, no per-flag migration hint (`.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts:574-581`). (3) `CLAUDE.md` belongs to the `claude` module. (4) Tracker switching is free; `--force` does not affect install and is uninstall-only: it deletes owned whole-file files even if consumer-modified (`.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts:523-528`). (5) `bkit status` verb. (6) `bkit upgrade` is scoped to modules detected on disk by `detectInstalledModules` (`.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts:1273-1287`): core always, each host by its `agents/` directory (`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.opencode/`, `.codex/`), `lint` by `.bkit/scripts/bkit-slop-type-suppression.mjs`. There is no `bkit.installedModules` field, so deleting a host directory narrows the next upgrade.
rationale: A bare `bkit install` installing everything was a footgun for partial installs — consumers that want only Claude Code got Cursor hooks they didn't request. Requiring an explicit `--claude` flag to receive `CLAUDE.md` matches the additive-host model: each host module owns its own agent-launcher file. Dropping `--force` for tracker switches reflects the tracker-pluggability work (#39) where switching is now lossless and always safe.

summary: BAR-139 — `.bkit/version` is a JSON object whose hash map lets uninstall delete an owned file only while it is unchanged
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** `.bkit/version` is a JSON object `{ pinnedVersion, canonicalHashes, claudeAllowDerived }` (`.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts`). `canonicalHashes` maps each owned file bkit wrote to the sha256 of what it wrote. `bkit uninstall` deletes an owned whole-file only when its on-disk content matches the recorded hash; a consumer-modified file, or one with no hash, stays unless `--force` / `--nuke`. bkit writes no template into the repo, so templates carry no hash and uninstall never deletes an adopted copy; `RETIRED_MANAGED_PATHS` (`.bkit/src/bkit-retire.ts`) drops hashes older installs recorded for them. A plain-text payload parses as `{ pinnedVersion, canonicalHashes: {} }` (unknown → preserve). A `tier3Hashes` map in an older file is read, folded under `canonicalHashes` (a canonical entry wins), and dropped at the next install or upgrade (`.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts:19-22`); a `webFetchDerived` list is read as `claudeAllowDerived`.
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-139, DE-10, `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-uninstall.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-retire.ts`
rationale: An owned file is deleted during uninstall only if it is still exactly what bkit wrote. Without a recorded hash, `bkit uninstall` cannot tell an unedited copy (safe to delete) from a consumer-customised one (must stay). Plain text cannot hold the map; JSON is human-readable and extensible.
alternatives: (1) Keep plain text and detect default content by re-rendering the template at uninstall — fails for files with token substitution bkit can no longer re-compute (consumer tokens may have changed). (2) Store hashes in a separate file — two files to keep in sync; `.bkit/version` is the natural home.

summary: BAR-141 — Structured PreflightFinding replaces printSink
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Replace `ModuleContext.printSink: string[]` with `ModuleContext.advisories: PreflightFinding[]` (shape: `{id, severity, detect, action}`). Install restructured into three phases: Phase 1 preflight (read-only, blockers short-circuit before any writes), Phase 2 dispatch (unchanged), Phase 3 post-install re-detection (token surfaces, ci.yml, vale sync). Findings deduplicated by `id` — Phase 3 wins on conflict.
- **Why:** `printSink: string[]` was unparseable by downstream tooling, emitted advisory strings during module execution (before post-install state was accurate), and had no structured `id` for deduplication. Structured shape enables: (1) stable `id` registry for downstream automation; (2) blocker short-circuit before any writes; (3) accurate post-install re-detection; (4) unified banner formatter reusable by BAR-139 (`bkit uninstall`).
- **Discarded:** (1) Keep `printSink` + add parallel `findings: PreflightFinding[]` — two sinks → drift risk; downstream tooling has to merge two shapes. (2) `--strict` flag promoting advisories to blockers — out of scope; consumer can use `bkit check` (exit-1-on-drift). (3) Auto-apply advisory fixes — violates consumer-value-wins principle.
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-141, `docs/plans/202605/bar-141-preflight-checklist-plan.md`, `.bkit/src/bkit-preflight.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-tiers.ts`, DE-3, KN-4
rationale: `printSink: string[]` was unparseable by downstream tooling, emitted advisory strings during module execution (before post-install state was accurate), and had no structured `id` for deduplication. Structured shape enables: (1) stable `id` registry for downstream automation; (2) blocker short-circuit before any writes; (3) accurate post-install re-detection; (4) unified banner formatter reusable by BAR-139 (`bkit uninstall`).

summary: #245 — opencode is a first-class host (Approach B); `bkit mode` and the ccr router are retired
description: opencode is installed with `bkit install --opencode=<provider>` (providers: see `opencode-provider-allowlist-cut-to-four`). Every host is an explicit flag — `--claude`, `--cursor`, `--codex`, `--opencode=<provider>` — and a bare `bkit install` exits 1; nothing is always-on. `bkit mode`, `bkit-mode.sh` and claude-code-router are gone; the `bkit-mode-sh-deletion-required` advisory cleans up old installs.
rationale: opencode is a first-class OpenAI-format harness (subagents, hooks, plugins, MCP) — no proxy/router required. Adding it as a third render target beside claude/cursor is the correct long-term model: one codebase, many hosts. The ccr router was always a bridging hack (Anthropic API → OpenAI format); a native host eliminates the mismatch and the `source ~/.zshrc` ceremony. `.bkit/scripts/bkit-mode.sh` was written once and never overwritten by upgrade, so every prior consumer still has it on disk — the drift-detect + deletion advisory (KN-33 pattern) ensures they are guided to clean up without silent data loss.

references: docs/deployments.md § CI trigger on final workflow push
summary: #141 — bkit-cloud rebuilt on the Claude GitHub App
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Rebuild the GitHub-tracker cloud capability **on** the Claude GitHub App rather than around `github.token`. (1) **Auth = Claude App via OIDC:** `bkit-cloud.yml` grants `id-token: write`; `claude-code-action@v1` authenticates as the App; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` stays (LLM). Delete the "`github.token` handles all repo git/gh; no App" framing. (2) **App = base requirement** for `cloud=claude` (advisory + `bkit check` consistency, not a runtime API probe — a specific App's install isn't reliably detectable from a user PAT). (3) **`cloud=claude`/`cloud=cursor` module split** mirroring `tracker=`: explicit `--cloud=claude|cursor` (not auto-derived), **tracker-constrained** (github→claude, linear→cursor; symmetric mismatch hard-error). (4) **Enforcement off `package.json` recorded state** (`bkit.issueTracker` + `bkit.cloudAgents` field, value `"claude"|"cursor"|"opencode"|"none"` — no separate `bkit.cloud` field): tracker switching is free; a cloud variant whose tracker does not match exits 1 with a re-run hint. (5) **Triggers:** design/plan/build + manual ship/debug via `@claude /bkit-<phase>` (typed command = phase) wired in `claude.yml`; auto ship/debug via `bkit-cloud.yml` `workflow_run`, two-tier gated; bare issue assignment is NOT a phase carrier. (6) **Two-tier CI auto-route gate:** free tier = job `if:` on commit marker `bkit [auto route]` (zero runner minutes when absent); cheap tier = in-job `gh issue view --json labels` re-check of `bkit:auto` (live kill switch). Gate logic lives in YAML (`bkit:start/end`), phase routing + status.json + comments stay in the orchestrator. (7) **Marker `bkit [auto route]`** (`bkit` outside brackets, per `bkit [skip ci]`) on close-workflow + debug re-trigger commits, only when the issue carried `bkit:auto` at close time. Folds defects D1 (missing `id-token`), D2 (`worktree-setup`/`create-pr` lack `[skip ci]` → mid-build router fire), D3 (incoherent concurrency key → dispatch/CI race; reconcile to one FID-derived token). Couples with #184 (shared HEAD-subject assertion = SoT for the commit-tag contract; treats `bkit [auto route]` as legitimate, not a skip tag) — must land together. Drops the vestigial Linear render branch (`bkit-cloud.yml` is GitHub-only) and migrates Linear bare `Auto` → `bkit:auto`.
- **Why:** A live dispatch proved the CI-driven path never ran end-to-end (OIDC boot failure). Building on the App reuses identity, PR/issue context, comment posting, and `@claude` follow-ups instead of reinventing them; bkit adds only phase routing, opt-in gate, stale guard, status.json. Two-tier gating gives a free kill switch (zero runner minutes for non-opted-in commits) plus a live runtime kill switch.
- **Discarded:** (1) `github_token` bypass of the App — superseded; breaks `@claude` follow-ups and reinvents App surface. (2) Runtime App-presence detection from a user PAT — unreliable; use recorded-state + advisory + `bkit check`. (3) Auto-derive `--cloud` variant from tracker — explicit value required; tracker constrains but does not select. (4) Linear→`repository_dispatch`→`bkit-cloud` bridge — dropped; Linear cloud routing is Cursor-native.
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** #141 (FINAL SCOPE `issuecomment-4542046671`), #184, #119, #138, #139, `.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml` + `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml`, `.github/workflows/claude.yml`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts` (`runCloudModule`/`MODULE_REGISTRY`), `.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts`, `.bkit/workflows/bkit-{build,debug,ship,auto}.md`, `.bkit/cloud.md`, `.bkit/trackers.md`, `.bkit/templates/.claude/hooks/preflight.sh`, `.bkit/templates/.cursor/hooks/preflight.sh`, `docs/deployments.md` § CI trigger on final workflow push, DE-14, DE-15, KN-11
- **Current (checked 2026-10-09):** `--cloud=` was dropped outright (#252), not kept as an alias — `.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts` rejects it as an unknown flag; the variant flag is `--auto=claude|cursor|opencode`. Tracker switching is free and `--force` is uninstall-only (`.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts:523-528`); `--auto=cursor` needs tracker=linear, `--auto=claude` / `--auto=opencode` need tracker=github (`validateCloudTrackerMatch`, `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts:1347`). `bkit.cloudAgents` values are `CLOUD_MODES` (`.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts:100`). The orchestrator is `.bkit/workflows/bkit-auto.md`; the GHA file is still `.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: A live dispatch proved the CI-driven path never ran end-to-end (OIDC boot failure). Building on the App reuses identity, PR/issue context, comment posting, and `@claude` follow-ups instead of reinventing them; bkit adds only phase routing, opt-in gate, stale guard, status.json. Two-tier gating gives a free kill switch (zero runner minutes for non-opted-in commits) plus a live runtime kill switch.

summary: Claude + opencode cloud dispatch share one bkit-cloud.yml as two runtime-gated jobs
description: Both CI dispatch jobs live in a single `bkit-cloud.yml` template (`.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml`), which the consumer copies and owns, each independently gated on its own secret (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for claude, OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY for opencode). One secret set means one job runs; both set means both run additively. The opencode job dispatches headlessly via opencode run, reading provider config from the committed .opencode/opencode.json, with the single OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY fanned out to every known provider env var name so the config {env:VAR} reference resolves whichever provider is installed.
rationale: one file is one audit surface and one template to copy. Runtime-gated jobs are idempotent — the second job is a near-instant no-op until the consumer adds its secret, so no consumer pays for a host they do not run.
alternatives: a separate opencode-cloud.yml file, or a separate CLI flag path treating the opencode host as a later phase — both double the template/audit surface for jobs that already no-op without their secret

summary: bkit owns only what a workflow step runs or parses; every shipped file is an owned file, an owned part of a shared file, create-if-missing, or a template
description: **Owned file** — install and upgrade overwrite it; uninstall removes it while it still matches its `.bkit/version` hash: workflow, prompt, agent and command copies, `docs/templates/bkit-plan.md` and `docs/templates/bkit-audit-*.md`, `.bkit/.env.example`, `.bkit/scripts/bkit-slop-type-suppression.mjs`, and the hook scripts (`.claude/hooks/*`, `.codex/hooks/*`, `.cursor/hooks/*`, `.opencode/plugin/gateguard.js`). **Owned part of a shared file** — bkit rewrites and removes only its part: markdown between `bkit:start` and `bkit:end` (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/rules.md`, `.agents/docs.md`, `docs/*.md`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`); hook entries and permissions in `.claude/settings.json`; Cursor and Codex `hooks.json`; `permission`, `plugin`, `mcp` and `provider` in `.opencode/opencode.json`; the tracker entry under `mcpServers` in `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`. **Create if missing** — written once when absent, no hash, no message, skipped by upgrade, left by uninstall: `.agents/context.md`, `.agents/skills.md` (`CREATE_IF_MISSING_PATHS`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:274`) and the `bkit:gate:*` / `bkit:deps:*` names in `package.json`. **Template** — never applied to the repo; raw copies refresh in the consumer's `.bkit/templates/` (`isTemplate`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:283-311`). No file is written once and then hash-tracked: bkit either keeps a file current or leaves it to the consumer.
rationale: A file a workflow step runs or parses has to match the workflows, so bkit keeps it current; a file a person or another tool runs belongs to the consumer's stack, so it ships as a template (issue body). The write-once, hash, upgrade-conflict and uninstall-reclaim machinery existed only so bkit could claim a consumer's file still matched the installed version; once the consumer decides whether to adopt, that claim is gone (issue body). Hooks stay owned because they enforce what workflows and prompts forbid (force push, `--no-verify`, `git reset --hard`) and change in step with them, so a stale copy runs workflows under old guards with no signal. The JSON keys stay owned because install fills them from install choices (`@@OPENCODE_TRACKER_MCP@@`, `@@OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY@@`), the tracker MCP entry is what tracker steps write through, and these files change often (settled plan 2026-10-07 §1). Accepted cost: bkit no longer promises that a consumer's CI, hooks and prose-lint config match the installed version, so workflows must not call those files (`467-workflows-reach-templates-only-via-commands-and-package-json-settings`).
alternatives: The issue body's boundary table, with MCP config and the gate scripts on the template side — rejected in the 2026-10-07 settled plan as too coarse: tracker steps need the tracker MCP entry, workflows run the gate scripts, and the table missed that workflows still called some template files (those calls were removed first, in #467).

summary: Install and upgrade copy the template set raw into the consumer's `.bkit/templates/`; upgrade lists changed, added and removed paths; bkit keeps no hash of, and makes no claim about, an adopted copy
description: `isTemplate` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:283-311`) is the one template list: `.github/renovate.json5`, `.github/dependabot.yml`, `.github/workflows/renovate.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml`, `.husky/pre-commit`, `.husky/pre-push`, `.vale.ini`, `.vale/styles/House/*`, `.lintstagedrc.json`, `slop-scan.config.json`, `.prettierignore`, `.envrc`, `.cursor/settings.json`, `.cursor/environment.json`, `.cursor/Dockerfile`, `.graphifyignore`, `.serena/project.yml`, `docs/capabilities.md`, and everything under `scripts/`. `syncTemplateCopies` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:567`) copies those package bytes unchanged, `{{...}}` placeholders included, keeps the file mode, and deletes a copy that left the set; it is a no-op in bkit's own repo. Upgrade compares old and new bytes before overwriting and prints the changed / added / removed paths with a pointer to `.bkit/templates.md` (`.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts:2177-2184`). `bkit check` reports a `.bkit/templates/` copy that differs from the package; uninstall removes `.bkit/templates/` and never an adopted copy. Template paths carry no `.bkit/version` hash; `RETIRED_MANAGED_PATHS` (`.bkit/src/bkit-retire.ts`) drops hashes older installs recorded for them and keeps the consumer's file. Every template that takes a comment opens with "Example. Copy into the repo and own it." The `.prettierignore`, `.vale.ini` and `slop-scan.config.json` templates ignore `.bkit/templates/`; a consumer gate that scans the whole repo ignores it too (`.bkit/templates.md:26-27`).
rationale: A one-line "templates were updated" notice on every release gets skipped, so upgrade names the paths. The list says "these paths changed in this version", not "your copy is behind": no per-file ownership record and no drift hash (issue body). The consumer's `.bkit/templates/` is bkit's own folder, so writing there keeps the rule that bkit never writes the consumer's files; before this, templates existed only under `node_modules/@cbartens/bkit/`, so copy-from paths in the docs were wrong for consumers (settled plan 2026-10-07 §3). Comparing bytes before overwriting needs no hash record and no release-time list (settled plan §3). Copies stay raw so they are the package bytes and `git diff .bkit/templates` on an upgrade commit is the template changelog (`syncTemplateCopies` header, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:560-566`).
alternatives: (1) One "templates were updated" line per release — rejected: it gets skipped (issue body). (2) A per-file record or drift hash for adopted copies — rejected (issue body). (3) Split the package into `.bkit/install/` (owned sources) and `.bkit/templates/` (templates only), proposed 2026-10-07 §10 — rejected 2026-10-09: it gives consumers the same result at the cost of moving every install path constant and test fixture; the package's `.bkit/templates/` stays mixed and only `isTemplate` paths are copied. (4) Name the template folder `examples/` — not adopted: it contradicts the owner's "`.bkit/templates/` holds all templates" (issue comment, settled plan §10). (5) Fill placeholders in the copies — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10): a filled copy is no longer the package bytes.

summary: bkit adds no tool `package.json` scripts, devDependencies or Husky wiring; core seeds only the `bkit:gate:*` / `bkit:deps:*` names, add-if-missing
description: bkit does not add `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `lint:prose`, `lint:slop`, `slop:delta`, the devDependencies `prettier`, `slop-scan`, `lint-staged`, `husky`, or `"prepare": "husky"`; they belong in `.bkit/templates.md`, in each template's install steps. The `git-hooks` module does not exist; `.husky/pre-commit` and `.husky/pre-push` are templates. Core runs `seedCorePackageJsonScripts` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:972`) at install and upgrade: each `BKIT_GATE_SCRIPTS` name (`.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts:393`) that is missing is added with its default value; a name already present is never touched, whatever its value; a missing name counts as a `bkit check` write. Install and upgrade still re-point a `slop:delta` or `lint:prose` value that byte-matches one an older bkit wrote (`LEGACY_SLOP_DELTA_SCRIPTS`, `LEGACY_LINT_PROSE_SCRIPTS`, `.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts`). The `gate-missing-called-scripts` and `gate-tier-not-wired` advisories run in core (`detectGateAdvisories`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:1015`) and point at `.bkit/templates.md`. bkit manages no `package.json` script value or devDependency, so uninstall leaves `package.json` alone and has no `--package` or `--keep-tooling` flag. `--typescript` writes only `.bkit/scripts/bkit-slop-type-suppression.mjs`.
rationale: Workflows, prompts and hooks run only the `bkit:gate:*` / `bkit:deps:*` scripts, so those names are what bkit needs present, and the consumer owns what each one runs (settled plan 2026-10-07 §1). The tool scripts are run by a person, a hook or another tool, never by a workflow, so they fall on the template side of the boundary (issue body). `package.json` becomes the one place that defines what "the checks" are, and workflows, pre-push and `.agents/rules.md` point at it (settled plan §5). Accepted cost: a `bkit:gate:static` of `echo ok` turns every agent run and push green; the gates audit flags every `bkit:gate:*` script that is missing, empty or cannot fail, and ignoring a finding is a REJECT row in `docs/decisions.jsonl` (settled plan §6, 3a6561b6). The legacy re-point stays because it rescues callers of a retired script (owner, 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Keep seeding the tool scripts and devDependencies — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10); no reason beyond the boundary rule is written down. Keep the gate names in a module's `packageJsonKeys` so uninstall removes them — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10): they are create-if-missing, which uninstall leaves; no further reason is written down.

summary: `--ci`, `--tooling`, the `ci` module and the `git-hooks` module are removed outright, with no deprecation window
description: `--ci` and `--tooling` are unknown flags: each exits 1 with the generic `[bkit] Unknown flag` error and no migration hint (`.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts:574-581`). The accepted module flags are `--claude`, `--cursor`, `--codex`, `--opencode=<provider>` and `--typescript` (`.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts:237`). There is no `ci` module, no `ci.yml` skeleton variant and no `git-hooks` module; the `ci.yml` template ships only the wired form. A consumer copies `ci.yml`, `.vale.ini` and the Husky hooks from `.bkit/templates/`.
rationale: Once `ci.yml` and `.vale.ini` became templates the `ci` module had nothing left to write, and `--tooling` only meant `--ci --typescript` (fd580708). The owner chose removal now over a deprecation window (2026-10-10); no reason for skipping a window is written down.
alternatives: Keep `--ci` for a release as a deprecated no-op or warning — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10); no reason recorded. Keep the derived `ci.yml` skeleton (TypeScript steps commented out) for non-Node repos — dropped with the `ci` module (owner, 2026-10-10); no reason recorded.

summary: `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`: bkit owns only its tracker entry under `mcpServers`; the rest of the file is the consumer's
description: bkit owns exactly one key in `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`: `mcpServers[<tracker>]`. Install and upgrade set it to the template's entry for the recorded tracker and keep every other server and its order (`reconcileMcpJson`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:2299`); a new file holds only the tracker entry (tracker none → empty map). Uninstall removes only bkit's entry, only while it still equals the template, and deletes the file when nothing is left (`.bkit/install.md:459`). A malformed file stops install. Same per-key replace as `.opencode/opencode.json`.
rationale: Tracker writes go only through MCP, so the tracker entry is what makes tracker steps work; bkit already replaced single keys in `opencode.json`, and these configs change often (settled plan 2026-10-07 §1).
alternatives: MCP config as a template, as the issue body's boundary table had it — rejected 2026-10-07: a stale or missing tracker entry breaks tracker steps. Whole-file ownership — not adopted: the settled plan gives the rest of the file to the consumer; no further reason is written down.

summary: Record files are created by the commands that first write them; install never creates them
description: `docs/failures.jsonl`, `docs/deferrals.jsonl`, `docs/roadmap.md`, `.bkit/issues.jsonl`, `.bkit/friction.jsonl` and `.bkit/stats.jsonl` are not install outputs: the step or command that first appends a row creates the file (`bkit roadmap feature` renders `docs/roadmap.md`). `.bkit/src/bkit-install.integration.test.ts:438` pins that install never creates `docs/roadmap.md`. Only `.agents/context.md`, `.agents/skills.md` and the `bkit:gate:*` / `bkit:deps:*` names are create-if-missing.
rationale: Not written down: the owner chose lazy creation on 2026-10-10 over the 2026-10-07 plan, and the record states the choice without a reason.
alternatives: Create the record files if missing at install (settled plan 2026-10-07 §1) — not adopted 2026-10-10; no reason recorded.

summary: `bkit.runners` and the `CLOUD_RUNNER` / `NODE_VERSION` install tokens are deleted; the consumer fills placeholders in their own copy
description: There is no `bkit.runners` `package.json` key and no runner-label or Node-version token. Template copies keep their placeholders: `{{CLOUD_RUNNER}}` in both `bkit-cloud.yml` jobs' `runs-on`, `{{NODE_VERSION}}` and `{{DEFAULT_BRANCH}}` in `ci.yml`. Placeholder guidance belongs in `.bkit/templates.md`; the cloud setup advisory names `{{CLOUD_RUNNER}}` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:2366-2370`), and `docs/deployments.md:423` says to edit `runs-on` in the copy.
rationale: The key and tokens existed only to fill `bkit-cloud.yml` and `ci.yml`, which bkit no longer writes (fd580708).
alternatives: Keep `bkit.runners` and fill the placeholders in the `.bkit/templates/` copies — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10): a filled copy is no longer the package bytes, so `git diff .bkit/templates` stops being the template changelog (`syncTemplateCopies` header, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:560-566`).

summary: `/bkit-build` Step 4 (plan currency) is advisory on every verdict; a `Broken` task never stops the build
description: `@bkit-build-plan-current` returns PASS / CONCERNS / FAIL and every value routes to Step 5 (`.bkit/workflows/bkit-build.md:441`). CONCERNS / FAIL are recorded on the `step-done` row, posted to the tracker with `Affected`, and echoed as a console advisory (`.bkit/workflows/bkit-build.md:436-438`). `@bkit-build-plan-execute` reads `build-plan-current.md` as fact about the codebase and the plan as intent. Build never revises the plan file; `/bkit-plan` does, and its close re-stamps the anchor (`.bkit/workflows.md:651`).
rationale: Stopping a build over plan drift costs more than building on: the usual `Broken` finding is work that already landed, and the fix (a `/bkit-plan` re-run) throws away a worktree that was ready to build (88638a42). The findings go to plan-execute instead of stopping the run.
alternatives: FAIL → Failure Path, the routing #431 first shipped (ec0012e5) — replaced in 88638a42 for the reason above.

summary: Ledger rows carry no alias or identity field: `ts` is the id, `key` the content slug, and every pointer, legacy `DE-N` / `KN-N` included, goes in `references[]`
description: `references[]` is the one cross-entry pointer field on every kind (`TelemetryEnvelope.references`, `.bkit/src/bkit-telemetry.ts:164-175`; `docs/architecture.md:172`). Keys are minted from content, never from a counter (`.bkit/jsonl.md` § Key & References). `bkit telemetry normalise` folds a legacy `aliases[]` field into `references[]` and re-keys only colliding rows; `bkit telemetry validate` exits 1 when one `DE-<n>` / `KN-<n>` is claimed by more than one key (#361).
rationale: Sequential `DE-{N}` ids cannot be issued safely when several runs mint ids at once: two runs read the same highest number from their own base commit and mint the same id, and `merge=union` keeps both rows without a conflict. Nine ids collided in a live consumer ledger, so an alias could not serve as a reliable identity (ca30d180).
alternatives: A separate `aliases[]` identity field beside the link field, as the #234 design had it — folded into `references[]` in ca30d180 for the reason above.

summary: Workflows, prompts and git hooks run local checks only through named `bkit:gate:*` `package.json` scripts; no prompt or workflow probes the toolchain itself
description: `BKIT_GATE_SCRIPTS` (`.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts:385`) is one chain: each gate is its parent plus one tier, named after the `ci.yml` job ids. The consumer owns every value; bkit only checks whether a name is declared. `/bkit-build` and `/bkit-debug` run the deepest declared gate and record its name; the integration / e2e / live gates are not seeded. The `.husky/pre-commit` / `.husky/pre-push` templates run the same names; `ci.yml` calls the tool scripts directly. `.bkit/src/bkit-local-gate-audit.test.ts` pins every call site.
rationale: Eight prompts and two workflows each carried their own `if [ -f turbo.json ] … else jq -e …` probe for the lint, typecheck and test command. A repo on another toolchain matched none of the probed names, got an empty command, `eval ""` exited 0, and the agent recorded a gate that ran nothing (24caa814). The probes also never ran `slop:delta` or `lint`, so agents passed a weaker gate than pre-push and CI. One named script per gate, shared by agents and hooks, makes a green agent gate and a green push run the same checks.
alternatives: Per-prompt toolchain probes — removed in 24caa814 for the reason above. A `bkit:lane:*` layer under the gates — collapsed into one chain in 2eda93b3: `bkit:gate:static` was a pure alias of `bkit:lane:static`, nothing read a lane name outside the manifest, and `ci.yml` never called the lane scripts.

summary: `lint:prose` soft-skips only when the `vale` binary is missing; missing `write-good` styles are restored, and a failed restore warns loudly
description: `LINT_PROSE_SCRIPT` (`.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts:319`; the template value in `.bkit/templates.md:68`): vale absent → one skip line, exit 0 (the F9 / BAR-138 soft-skip). Vale present but `.vale/styles/write-good` absent → copy it from the main worktree via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, else `vale sync`; still absent → `WARNING - PROSE LINT SKIPPED` on stderr. `LEGACY_LINT_PROSE_SCRIPTS` (`.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts:330`) lists values an older bkit wrote; install and upgrade re-point a byte-matching value and leave any other value alone.
rationale: `.vale/styles/write-good` is gitignored, so it is absent in every fresh clone and every `git worktree add`. The older guard treated that like a missing binary and exited 0 with one quiet line, so the prose gate turned itself off in worktrees while reporting success (a62dc54d). Missing styles can be restored; a missing binary cannot, and the soft-skip keeps bkit from failing a consumer's commit over a tool bkit does not install. The legacy list exists because the script was add-if-missing: without a re-point, an existing consumer would keep the self-disabling value forever (a62dc54d).

summary: Triage severity is `CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW`, required on friction / deferral / failure rows and absent on every other kind
description: `VALID_SEVERITIES` (`.bkit/src/bkit-telemetry.ts:228`), enforced by `validate()` on append. Same vocabulary the challenge prompts assign, so `@bkit-build-challenge-remediate` carries a blocked finding's severity into its deferral row unchanged. `bkit telemetry migrate` maps legacy `critical` → CRITICAL, `normal` → MEDIUM, `low` → LOW, and a missing value → MEDIUM (`mapLegacySeverity`, `.bkit/src/bkit-telemetry-migrate.ts:164`). Contract: `.bkit/jsonl.md` § Severity.
rationale: The legacy `critical | normal | low` scale carried no signal: authors left it at its default, 19 low / 2 normal / 0 critical of the 21 rows in the old `docs/pending.md` (ca30d180). Reusing the challenge prompts' scale lets a finding's severity pass through without being judged again.
alternatives: Keep the legacy `critical | normal | low` scale — dropped in ca30d180 for the reason above. Preflight `blocker` / `advisory` — a different axis; it gates `bkit install`.

summary: Workflow close telemetry, including the `rows` / `malformed` / `versions` ledger line, comes from one TypeScript implementation; no workflow computes it in bash
description: `workflowTelemetry` (`.bkit/src/bkit-telemetry.ts:1084`) builds the per-workflow report; `ledgerLine` (`.bkit/src/bkit-telemetry.ts:1067`) prints `[bkit-telemetry] ledger: N rows · malformed: M · versions: …` from the parse result. Callers: `bkit workflows close` (`.bkit/src/commands/workflow/workflows.ts:663`) and `bkit telemetry summary [--phase]` (`.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts:1746`).
rationale: The five workflows each carried their own bash copy of the summary, and each was wrong: `grep -c … || echo 0` printed `0\n0` on every clean run, because grep exits 1 on zero matches; `jq '.bkitVersion // "unknown"'` put empty versions under an empty key, because `//` substitutes only on null / false; `wc -l` counted lines, not parsed rows (cb19d6bc). One implementation counting parsed rows gives one answer.
alternatives: Per-workflow inline bash summaries — removed in cb19d6bc for the reason above.

summary: `bkit telemetry migrate` puts each legacy field in its own row field: heading → `summary`, Description → `description`, Discarded → `alternatives`, Related / Superseded by → `references`
description: In `.bkit/src/bkit-telemetry-migrate.ts`: `Discarded:` → `DecisionPayload.alternatives` (:536-537); deferral and friction rows take the heading as `summary` and the Description prose as `description` (:722-724, :790-792); the entry's own legacy id, then its `**Related:**` and `Superseded by:` pointers, go to `references` (:554-559); Severity goes through `mapLegacySeverity`; Status through the shared `parseLegacyStatus`.
rationale: The migrator used to drop content without saying so (026b6a43). `alternatives` was never filled because `Discarded:` was never parsed, which left 26 of bkit's 34 decision rows with their alternatives as prose inside `description`. Deferral and friction rows used the heading as `description` and threw the parsed prose away, keeping about 40% of the legacy content.
alternatives: Heading as `description` with no `summary` field on deferral / friction payloads — replaced in 026b6a43; the payloads had no `summary` field, so heading and prose could not both survive.

summary: bkit's own CI runs a direct push to `dev` at full depth; a push from a merged PR runs light
description: `bkit-tests-scope` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:117-136` asks `repos/{repo}/commits/{sha}/pulls`: a merged PR behind the commit → `run_level=light`; none → `full` (`ran-because:dev-push-direct-escalated`); API error → `full` (run-to-be-safe). Needs `pull-requests: read` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:10-11`). Documented in `docs/testing.md:674` and `docs/deployments.md:155`.
rationale: A merged-PR push is light because the PR already ran the full suite on that change; a direct push has no PR run behind it, so it gets the full run. The ci.yml comments called this "the uuid-incident fix" (d7cc47e2, backported from consumer-a #403). What the uuid incident was is not written down: neither bkit's nor consumer-a's git history, docs or `docs/knowledge.jsonl` describe it.

summary: Recovered import edges are written into `graph.json` by one writer, `bkit-graph-repair.py`; every other graph script only reads the file
description: `bkit-graph-repair.py` is the only caller of `resolved_import_edges()` (`scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-imports.py:11-15`) and runs inside every `pnpm graph*` wrapper between `extract` and `cluster-only` (`scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-repair.py:8-9`). Each injected link carries `"_origin": "graph-repair"`; a re-run adds nothing. `bkit-graph-eager.py` and `bkit-graphify-rollup.py` read the graph and call `warn_if_unrepaired()`. Same in the template copies under `.bkit/templates/scripts/graphify/`.
rationale: When each reader re-derived the edges on read, there were two answers to which edges exist, and `collapse()` needed a subtraction whose only job was to stop double counting (the deleted header text in 14e2a557). Repairing on read also leaves `graphify affected`, `god-nodes`, `explain`, `path` and `query` on a graph missing those edges, because they read `graph.json` directly; `affected` is the one most likely to be trusted in a hurry, and a missing edge looks like a clean result (`scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-repair.py:13-21`).
alternatives: Repair on read inside each reader — replaced for the reasons above.

summary: Drift rules scan two partitioned surfaces, `product` and `tests`; a rule with no `surface` key scans `product`
description: `bkit-graph-drift.py` puts every scanned file on exactly one surface: `tests` = files under an `e2e` directory or named `.test.` / `.spec.`; `product` = everything else, test helpers included (`scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-drift.py:73-91`). A rule picks `product` (default), `tests` or `all` (`:24-26`, `:112`). Same in `.bkit/templates/scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-drift.py`.
rationale: The test surface is exactly the set of files the product scan skips, so adding it moved no file and changed no existing rule's count, and therefore none of their exact budgets; the `product` default keeps that true for any rule without a `surface` key (the deleted header text in 14e2a557). The test surface exists because guards live in test code, which a product-only scan cannot see (`scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-drift.py:88-91`).

summary: #256 — managed version marker in rendered prompts/workflows; stale marker blocks on protected branches only
description: Every rendered `bkit-*.md` agent/command under the `.claude/`, `.cursor/` and `.opencode/` mirror dirs carries the managed version marker (`.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts`). A marker that differs from the installed version raises `bkit-rendered-prompts-stale`: `blocker` (exit 1) on a protected branch, `advisory` on a feature branch (`.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts`). Known gap: `.codex/agents/*.toml` carry no marker and are not scanned, so a stale Codex render passes silently.
rationale: Prior to v4.0.0 a consumer could silently run stale rendered files (e.g. workflows from v3 against a v4 binary that changed the wire protocol). The marker makes the installed version explicit in every file, and `bkit check` closes the gap between "version bumped in `package.json`" and "rendered files actually regenerated". The marker is placed at the top of every fully-managed file and is idempotent (one marker per file, overwritten on every re-render). The gate is a blocker only on `main` / `dev` (or a PR into them) and an advisory on a feature branch because a stale render on a feature branch usually comes from a version bump on the base branch that was not re-rendered in the same change, not from the feature branch itself (d2f17aa1). An undeterminable branch counts as protected, so an unknown environment never downgrades the gate (`isOnProtectedBranch`, `.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts:2273`).

summary: delete the SHIPPED_NETWORK_BASES fallback array from guardrails.cjs outright and make .cursor/allowlist.json the sole source, rather than generating the array at build time or keeping it hand-synced behind a parity test
description:
loadNetworkAllowlistBases starts from an empty Set and reads .cursor/allowlist.json alone. An empty set makes curlWgetHostAllowed return false for any parseable URL, so the hook ASKS. The ask message names .cursor/allowlist.json and bkit install so the degraded state is self-diagnosing. No two-entry safety floor is kept. The same doctrine is applied to the fourth copy: the WebFetch(domain:...) seed is emptied from .bkit/templates/.claude/settings.json, where it was already a stale partial subset that enrichClaudeSettingsAllows topped up invisibly.
- **Current (checked 2026-09-23):** The pre-existing `.bkit/src/bkit-permissions-parity.integration.test.ts` was kept and inverted, not deleted: it now asserts the hook carries no host list of its own and the shipped Claude settings seed no host grants.
rationale: Codegen recreates the exact failure this change exists to remove: a build step that can silently not run, leaving two copies drifting, and it couples a hash-gated shipped artifact to build ordering. A parity test automates the sync rather than eliminating it. The parity check that already existed for this pair (hook base list vs the WebFetch seed) was weak: both sides were hand-kept copies, so it could only catch the two drifting apart, never either drifting from the registry both claimed to mirror; its assertion is replaced, in the same test file, by checks that the hook holds no host list and the Claude settings template seeds no host grants (`.bkit/src/bkit-permissions-parity.integration.test.ts:396-410`). Deletion is safe because the hook and the artifact are written in the same runCursorModule pass and under the same upgrade gate, so the artifact exists whenever the hook does; and because an empty set degrades to ask, which is the fail-safe direction #394 established (guessing here converts an ask into an allow). No two-entry floor: two entries is still a hand-maintained list that can rot, and the case it guards cannot occur, since the hook only exists because bkit install put it there in the pass that wrote the artifact.
alternatives: codegen the array into the hook at pnpm build (rejected: silent non-execution is the exact drift vector being removed); keep the copies and forbid drift with a parity test (rejected: does not satisfy the issue, leaves a multi-file edit per provider forever, and is the shape of the assertion being deleted); keep a minimal github.com plus npmjs.com safety floor so a fresh clone does not ask on everything (rejected: still a hand-maintained list, and the case is unreachable)

summary: bkit owns only what a workflow step runs or parses; every shipped file is an owned file, an owned part of a shared file, create-if-missing, or a template
