description: **Owned file** — install and upgrade overwrite it; uninstall removes it while it still matches its `.bkit/version` hash: workflow, prompt, agent and command copies, `docs/templates/bkit-plan.md` and `docs/templates/bkit-audit-*.md`, `.bkit/.env.example`, `.bkit/scripts/bkit-slop-type-suppression.mjs`, and the hook scripts (`.claude/hooks/*`, `.codex/hooks/*`, `.cursor/hooks/*`, `.opencode/plugin/gateguard.js`). **Owned part of a shared file** — bkit rewrites and removes only its part: markdown between `bkit:start` and `bkit:end` (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/rules.md`, `.agents/docs.md`, `.agents/context.md`, `docs/*.md`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`); hook entries and permissions in `.claude/settings.json`; Cursor and Codex `hooks.json`; `permission`, `plugin`, `mcp` and `provider` in `.opencode/opencode.json`; the tracker entry under `mcpServers` in `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`. **Create if missing** — written once when absent, no hash, no message, skipped by upgrade, left by uninstall: `.agents/skills.md` (`CREATE_IF_MISSING_PATHS`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:274`) and the `bkit:gate:*` / `bkit:deps:*` names in `package.json`. **Template** — never applied to the repo; raw copies refresh in the consumer's `.bkit/templates/` (`isTemplate`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:282-312`), including one context-fetch file per provider under `.bkit/templates/context/`. No file is written once and then hash-tracked: bkit either keeps a file current or leaves it to the consumer.
rationale: A file a workflow step runs or parses has to match the workflows, so bkit keeps it current; a file a person or another tool runs belongs to the consumer's stack, so it ships as a template (issue body). The managed block of `.agents/context.md` holds the marker formats, self-skip contract and `allowed-domains` / `mcp-servers` rules that `/bkit-debug` and install parse, so bkit keeps it current; the ready-made fetch blocks are templates (`489-context-fetch-blocks-are-per-provider-templates`). The write-once, hash, upgrade-conflict and uninstall-reclaim machinery existed only so bkit could claim a consumer's file still matched the installed version; once the consumer decides whether to adopt, that claim is gone (issue body). Hooks stay owned because they enforce what workflows and prompts forbid (force push, `--no-verify`, `git reset --hard`) and change in step with them, so a stale copy runs workflows under old guards with no signal. The JSON keys stay owned because install fills them from install choices (`@@OPENCODE_TRACKER_MCP@@`, `@@OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY@@`), the tracker MCP entry is what tracker steps write through, and these files change often (settled plan 2026-10-07 §1). Accepted cost: bkit no longer promises that a consumer's CI, hooks and prose-lint config match the installed version, so workflows must not call those files (`467-workflows-reach-templates-only-via-commands-and-package-json-settings`).
alternatives: The issue body's boundary table, with MCP config and the gate scripts on the template side — rejected in the 2026-10-07 settled plan as too coarse: tracker steps need the tracker MCP entry, workflows run the gate scripts, and the table missed that workflows still called some template files (those calls were removed first, in #467). `.agents/context.md` as create-if-missing (Wave 2a, ef1f09a7) — reversed 2026-10-10 (owner, #489 "Decided (2026-10-10)"): its managed rules would freeze at the version first installed while the code that reads the blocks keeps changing.

summary: Install and upgrade copy the template set raw into the consumer's `.bkit/templates/`; upgrade lists changed, added and removed paths; bkit keeps no hash of, and makes no claim about, an adopted copy
description: `isTemplate` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:282-312`) is the one template list: `.github/renovate.json5`, `.github/dependabot.yml`, `.github/workflows/renovate.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml`, `.husky/pre-commit`, `.husky/pre-push`, `.vale.ini`, `.vale/styles/House/*`, `.lintstagedrc.json`, `slop-scan.config.json`, `.prettierignore`, `.envrc`, `.cursor/settings.json`, `.cursor/environment.json`, `.cursor/Dockerfile`, `.graphifyignore`, `.serena/project.yml`, `docs/capabilities.md`, everything under `context/` (one context-fetch file per provider) and everything under `scripts/`. `syncTemplateCopies` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:564`) copies those package bytes unchanged, `{{...}}` placeholders included, keeps the file mode, and deletes a copy that left the set; it is a no-op in bkit's own repo. Upgrade compares old and new bytes before overwriting and prints the changed / added / removed paths with a pointer to `.bkit/templates.md` (`.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts:2168-2173`). `bkit check` reports a `.bkit/templates/` copy that differs from the package; uninstall removes `.bkit/templates/` and never an adopted copy. Template paths carry no `.bkit/version` hash; `RETIRED_MANAGED_PATHS` (`.bkit/src/bkit-retire.ts`) drops hashes older installs recorded for them and keeps the consumer's file. Every template that takes a comment opens with "Example. Copy into the repo and own it." The `.prettierignore`, `.vale.ini` and `slop-scan.config.json` templates ignore `.bkit/templates/`; a consumer gate that scans the whole repo ignores it too (`.bkit/templates.md:47`).
rationale: A one-line "templates were updated" notice on every release gets skipped, so upgrade names the paths. The list says "these paths changed in this version", not "your copy is behind": no per-file ownership record and no drift hash (issue body). The consumer's `.bkit/templates/` is bkit's own folder, so writing there keeps the rule that bkit never writes the consumer's files; before this, templates existed only under `node_modules/@cbartens/bkit/`, so copy-from paths in the docs were wrong for consumers (settled plan 2026-10-07 §3). Comparing bytes before overwriting needs no hash record and no release-time list (settled plan §3). Copies stay raw so they are the package bytes and `git diff .bkit/templates` on an upgrade commit is the template changelog (`syncTemplateCopies` header, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:558-563`).
alternatives: (1) One "templates were updated" line per release — rejected: it gets skipped (issue body). (2) A per-file record or drift hash for adopted copies — rejected (issue body). (3) Split the package into `.bkit/install/` (owned sources) and `.bkit/templates/` (templates only), proposed 2026-10-07 §10 — rejected 2026-10-09: it gives consumers the same result at the cost of moving every install path constant and test fixture; the package's `.bkit/templates/` stays mixed and only `isTemplate` paths are copied. (4) Name the template folder `examples/` — not adopted: it contradicts the owner's "`.bkit/templates/` holds all templates" (issue comment, settled plan §10). (5) Fill placeholders in the copies — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10): a filled copy is no longer the package bytes.

summary: Record files are created by the commands that first write them; install never creates them
description: `docs/failures.jsonl`, `docs/deferrals.jsonl`, `docs/roadmap.md`, `.bkit/issues.jsonl`, `.bkit/friction.jsonl` and `.bkit/stats.jsonl` are not install outputs: the step or command that first appends a row creates the file (`bkit roadmap feature` renders `docs/roadmap.md`). `.bkit/src/bkit-install.integration.test.ts:438` pins that install never creates `docs/roadmap.md`. Only `.agents/skills.md` and the `bkit:gate:*` / `bkit:deps:*` names are create-if-missing.
rationale: Not written down: the owner chose lazy creation on 2026-10-10 over the 2026-10-07 plan, and the record states the choice without a reason.
alternatives: Create the record files if missing at install (settled plan 2026-10-07 §1) — not adopted 2026-10-10; no reason recorded.

summary: Ready-made context-fetch blocks ship as one template per provider in `.bkit/templates/context/`; the managed block of `.agents/context.md` holds only the rules
description: `.bkit/templates/context/` holds one file per provider: `github-ci`, `github-diff`, `playwright`, `maestro-ios`, `tavily`, `sentry`, `vercel`, `supabase`, `stripe`, `resend`, `inngest`, `cloudrun`, `expo`, `expo-workflows`, `serena`. Each file holds that provider's fetch block, its `context-fetch:provision` block where a stack CLI is needed, its env vars, the `allowed-domains` lines bkit's egress registry does not already derive, and its `mcp-servers` names. Project names, slugs and ids are placeholders (`your-team-slug`, `your-project-ref`, …) on a commented assignment line or env default, never a consumer's names (`.bkit/templates.md:76-92`, `.bkit/src/bkit-context-templates.test.ts:118`). `isTemplate` copies them raw into the consumer's `.bkit/templates/context/` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:307-308`). The managed block of `.agents/context.md` keeps only the rules — marker formats, contexts, self-skip contract, output bounds, provisioning, `allowed-domains` and `mcp-servers` — and bkit keeps it current. A consumer copies a provider's blocks below `<!-- bkit:end -->` and adds its domains and MCP names to their lists (`.bkit/templates.md:52-102`). The `context-fetch-source-not-enabled` advisory reads block names from these templates and names the file to copy (`shippedContextFetchTemplates`, `.bkit/src/bkit-preflight.ts`).
rationale: The managed half of `.agents/context.md` is the rules `/bkit-debug` and install parse; freezing it at first install leaves agents acting on stale rules while the code that reads the blocks moves on, so it stays bkit-owned and current. Examples are not rules, so they are templates the consumer adopts and owns. One file per provider, because the domains and MCP server names a block needs belong with that block. Folder `.bkit/templates/context/` is the owner's choice over the proposed `context-fetch/` (#489 "Decided (2026-10-10)"). Placeholders keep any one consumer's names out of shipped files (#489 proposal 2026-10-10).
alternatives: (1) `.agents/context.md` create-if-missing, examples kept inside its managed block (Wave 2a, ef1f09a7) — rejected: the rules freeze at the version first installed. (2) Separate allowed-domains and MCP-server templates — rejected: the hosts and servers a block needs belong with that block. (3) Folder `.bkit/templates/context-fetch/` — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10); no reason recorded.

summary: bkit adds no tool `package.json` scripts, devDependencies or Husky wiring; core seeds only the `bkit:gate:*` / `bkit:deps:*` names, add-if-missing
description: bkit does not add `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `lint:prose`, `lint:slop`, `slop:delta`, the devDependencies `prettier`, `slop-scan`, `lint-staged`, `husky`, or `"prepare": "husky"`; they belong in `.bkit/templates.md`, in each template's install steps. The `git-hooks` module does not exist; `.husky/pre-commit` and `.husky/pre-push` are templates. Core runs `seedCorePackageJsonScripts` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:969`) at install and upgrade: each `BKIT_GATE_SCRIPTS` name (`.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts:385`) that is missing is added with its default value; a name already present is never touched, whatever its value; a missing name counts as a `bkit check` write. Install and upgrade still re-point a `slop:delta` or `lint:prose` value that byte-matches one an older bkit wrote (`LEGACY_SLOP_DELTA_SCRIPTS`, `LEGACY_LINT_PROSE_SCRIPTS`, `.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts`). The `gate-missing-called-scripts` and `gate-tier-not-wired` advisories run in core (`detectGateAdvisories`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:1012`) and point at `.bkit/templates.md`. bkit manages no `package.json` script value or devDependency, so uninstall leaves `package.json` alone and has no `--package` or `--keep-tooling` flag. `--typescript` writes only `.bkit/scripts/bkit-slop-type-suppression.mjs`.
rationale: Workflows, prompts and hooks run only the `bkit:gate:*` / `bkit:deps:*` scripts, so those names are what bkit needs present, and the consumer owns what each one runs (settled plan 2026-10-07 §1). The tool scripts are run by a person, a hook or another tool, never by a workflow, so they fall on the template side of the boundary (issue body). `package.json` becomes the one place that defines what "the checks" are, and workflows, pre-push and `.agents/rules.md` point at it (settled plan §5). Accepted cost: a `bkit:gate:static` of `echo ok` turns every agent run and push green; the gates audit flags every `bkit:gate:*` script that is missing, empty or cannot fail, and ignoring a finding is a REJECT row in `docs/decisions.jsonl` (settled plan §6, 3a6561b6). The legacy re-point stays because it rescues callers of a retired script (owner, 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Keep seeding the tool scripts and devDependencies — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10); no reason beyond the boundary rule is written down. Keep the gate names in a module's `packageJsonKeys` so uninstall removes them — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10): they are create-if-missing, which uninstall leaves; no further reason is written down.

summary: `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`: bkit owns only its tracker entry under `mcpServers`; the rest of the file is the consumer's
description: bkit owns exactly one key in `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`: `mcpServers[<tracker>]`. Install and upgrade set it to the template's entry for the recorded tracker and keep every other server and its order (`reconcileMcpJson`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:2291`); a new file holds only the tracker entry (tracker none → empty map). Uninstall removes only bkit's entry, only while it still equals the template, and deletes the file when nothing is left (`.bkit/install.md:459`). A malformed file stops install. Same per-key replace as `.opencode/opencode.json`.
rationale: Tracker writes go only through MCP, so the tracker entry is what makes tracker steps work; bkit already replaced single keys in `opencode.json`, and these configs change often (settled plan 2026-10-07 §1).
alternatives: MCP config as a template, as the issue body's boundary table had it — rejected 2026-10-07: a stale or missing tracker entry breaks tracker steps. Whole-file ownership — not adopted: the settled plan gives the rest of the file to the consumer; no further reason is written down.

summary: `bkit.runners` and the `CLOUD_RUNNER` / `NODE_VERSION` install tokens are deleted; the consumer fills placeholders in their own copy
description: There is no `bkit.runners` `package.json` key and no runner-label or Node-version token. Template copies keep their placeholders: `{{CLOUD_RUNNER}}` in both `bkit-cloud.yml` jobs' `runs-on`, `{{NODE_VERSION}}` and `{{DEFAULT_BRANCH}}` in `ci.yml`. Placeholder guidance belongs in `.bkit/templates.md`; the cloud setup advisory names `{{CLOUD_RUNNER}}` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:2359-2362`), and `docs/deployments.md:423` says to edit `runs-on` in the copy.
rationale: The key and tokens existed only to fill `bkit-cloud.yml` and `ci.yml`, which bkit no longer writes (fd580708).
alternatives: Keep `bkit.runners` and fill the placeholders in the `.bkit/templates/` copies — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10): a filled copy is no longer the package bytes, so `git diff .bkit/templates` stops being the template changelog (`syncTemplateCopies` header, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:558-563`).

summary: GateGuard injects an investigation checklist on the first touch of each file, a reuse checklist on a new file, and a gate-config advisory on quality-gate configs; subagents are not exempt
description: Every host's GateGuard (`.claude/hooks/gateguard.cjs`, `.cursor/hooks/gateguard.cjs`, `.codex/hooks/gateguard.cjs`, `.opencode/plugin/gateguard.js`) advises once per (session, file): first touch gets the investigation checklist, a write to a missing path (Codex: `*** Add File:`) gets the reuse-over-duplicate checklist, a quality-gate config basename gets the fix-the-code advisory, and `docs/**/*.md` outside `docs/plans/` gets the docs authoring advisory appended. Subagent edits get the same treatment under their own session id. A multi-file Codex patch advises on its first not-yet-warned target.
rationale: LLM self-review is weak; the act of investigating before an edit is what changes the output. A write to a not-yet-existing path is where bolt-on drift is born, and the read-this-file checklist does not fit a file that does not exist yet. Editing a gate config to silence a gate is the recurring weaken-the-gate-instead-of-fixing-the-code anti-pattern. A subagent edit skips the same investigation an orchestrator edit would. `docs/plans/` is governed by the plan template, not the docs register. Advising on the first not-yet-warned Codex target stops a multi-file patch from burying a new file behind an already-seen one. Reasons moved out of the hook comments (owner rule 2026-10-10: comments state current state only).
alternatives: Exempt subagents — not adopted: same investigation skipped. Read-this-file checklist for new files — not adopted: does not fit a missing file.

summary: GateGuard is advisory by default with deny behind BKIT_GATEGUARD=deny, fails open through one top-level catch, and keeps its managed block a pure engine with no stdin/stdout
description: GateGuard never blocks unless BKIT_GATEGUARD=deny. Normal control paths use existence guards; one top-level catch is the only error sink and exits 0 (Cursor: bare allow). The managed block reads no stdin and writes no stdout/stderr; the driver below it emits exactly once. Session-state GC runs after the advisory is decided. `bkit-gateguard-parity.integration.test.ts` runs one behaviour table against every host.
rationale: The deny ramp is a deliberate, dogfood-gated flip: wired already so enabling it is a config change, not a code change. A hook that throws would break the consumer's session or stand between the agent and its edit. Two emitters (bkit's and the consumer's) on one stdout collide into one unparseable blob, which Cursor and Claude Code discard whole. GC runs last so a cleanup race cannot suppress the advisory. The parity table exists because getting the Codex tool name or the V4A envelope parser wrong leaves a hook that installs, exits 0 and silently never fires — a gate that proves only that it was asked. Reasons moved out of the hook comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Deny by default — not adopted pending dogfood. Per-call try/catch — not adopted: one error sink only.

summary: Shell guardrails flag off-allowlist curl/wget URL hosts and shell-as-edit-channel writes as advisories; Claude's hook never denies or asks; detection is head-of-segment, scheme-strict, host-only and quiet on scratch sinks
description: `.claude/hooks/guardrails.cjs` covers only what a command-prefix permission table cannot express: URL hosts and shell edits into source files. It emits `additionalContext` only. Cursor's twin asks on off-allowlist fetches and allows shell edits with an agent_message; Codex's emits its ask tier as advisory. All hosts match the program a segment runs (not a bare token), count only explicit-scheme URLs, consult only each URL's host, and report only redirects into repo-looking paths with source extensions.
rationale: Claude rules match a command prefix, never a URL host, and a blanket ask row would force a prompt on every shell fetch in every mode — unanswerable in a cloud session; the hook gives the signal without the prompt. `deny` already lives in settings.json and is evaluated before any hook, so a duplicate would be dead code with a second place to drift. A content-scoped `ask` is evaluated before the auto-mode classifier and always forces a prompt — the stall the host is configured to avoid. Shell edits stay advisory on every host because the edit-tools rule has sanctioned exceptions (bkit's plan workflow does a `sed -i.bak -E` bulk rewrite) and a gate that blocks a documented exception gets switched off. Matching a bare token fires on `grep 'curl'`, and a gate that fires on noise or constantly is one consumers disable. A scheme-less token cannot be told apart from a local path without guessing, and guessing turns a flag into an allow. Matching the allowlist against the whole command string is defeated by `?src=github.com` or `github.com.attacker.io`; the host alone decides where bytes go. On Codex the ask tier informs rather than stops; every command in it is already PROHIBITED in all bkit workflow headers, so only a human driving Codex by hand reaches it. Reasons moved out of the hook comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Ask row on Claude shell curl — rejected: prompt on every fetch. Block shell edits — rejected: sanctioned exceptions. Whole-string allowlist match — rejected: trivially defeated.

summary: cloud-bootstrap.sh re-checks workspace trust at the discovered git root and branches gh setup on the `gh auth status` probe, not on token presence
description: `.claude/hooks/cloud-bootstrap.sh` reads `.projects[<git root>].hasTrustDialogAccepted` from `~/.claude.json` and logs the snapshot fix when false. gh setup: gh absent → MCP lane only; `gh auth status` passes → untouched; GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN set but failing → log fault and fix; else `gh auth login --with-token` from BKIT_GH_TOKEN. RUNTIME_GITHUBCLI is always logged; the enforcing abort is the workflow Step-1 preflight.
rationale: Untrusted, every allow row is silently ignored and the only notice is a stderr line no cloud session surfaces, so the hook makes that no-op loud. The setup script's baked repo path is an observation of the current image, not a contract, so the discovered root is re-checked. Branching on presence would, in the placeholder-GH_TOKEN failure, decline the only repair the hook has and say nothing specific; preferring the sanctioned env lane means preferring it when it works. A present-but-broken env token cannot be repaired from the hook: `--with-token` would report success while gh keeps using the env value, and Claude Code documents no supported way to rewrite a cloud env var from a session. The Supabase example gates on the docker daemon because `command -v supabase` passes once a provision recipe installs the CLI while the container runtime is absent, and `supabase start || log` would swallow the failure into one stderr line. Reasons moved out of the hook comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Presence check on GH_TOKEN — rejected: misdiagnoses a placeholder token.

summary: Template pre-push runs only deterministic gates via the `bkit:gate*` scripts, skips the suite on revert branches, and blocks a [skip ci] HEAD on a branch with an open PR; bkit-repo pre-commit skips the dist check for test-only commits
description: `.bkit/templates/.husky/pre-push` runs the `bkit:gate*` scripts plus the drift gate; slow/network/deploy tiers stay in CI. On a revert branch the test suite is skipped while lint, typecheck, prose and slop:delta still run. A HEAD commit carrying a [skip ci]-class token is blocked when the branch has an open PR (dev/main exempt, gh absent → allow). bkit's own `.husky/pre-commit` runs `bkit:check:dist` only when a non-test `.bkit/src/*.ts` is staged; its pre-push bats run self-skips when bats is absent.
rationale: The hook mirrors CI's deterministic gates so a green push cannot red-CI on them, and keeping slow checks out stops a green push implying more than those gates verified. Gate content lives in package.json so a human push and an agent run enforce the identical set. A revert leaves the tree intentionally inconsistent (deleted files referenced by surviving tests), so the suite is skipped so recovery lands; prose is unaffected by deleted code and slop:delta reports removals as resolved, never added. The workflow CI-Dispatch gate only covers the push it makes at close; the HEAD guard backstops manual pushes, and is conditioned on an open PR so sanctioned [skip ci] pushes with no PR still pass. `bkit:check:dist` rebuilds from the working tree, so a test-only commit made while a source edit is uncommitted would fail on a diff it did not cause. bats is not a devDependency, and without the self-skip a contributor without bats could not push. Reasons moved out of the hook comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The slop-scan plugin flags escape-hatch casts, ts-* suppression directives, skipped/focused tests and blanket lint disables; the object-literal double cast weighs highest; per-rule next-line disables are not flagged
description: `.bkit/templates/.bkit/scripts/bkit-slop-type-suppression.mjs` emits `boundary/type-suppression` (double cast, any cast, ts-ignore / ts-nocheck / ts-expect-error) and `boundary/gate-suppression` (.skip / .only / x- / f-prefixed tests, blanket eslint disables). It pins `meta.apiVersion`, omits `delta`, and evades its own pattern literals.
rationale: A cast or suppression at a boundary lets a renamed SDK field or changed signature compile clean and ship broken while the boundary test passes against the wrong shape; the directives suppress the very error a boundary test exists to surface. The object-literal double cast is the shape that shipped consumer-b #122 / PR #282 silently broken, so it weighs highest. Skipped tests and blanket disables are the same weaken-the-gate reflex for non-type gates; the targeted per-rule next-line form is the doctrine's sanctioned opt-out. apiVersion is pinned so an engine API bump fails loud instead of running against a mismatched contract. Casts err toward under-flagging: a nag, not a wedge. Reasons moved out of the plugin comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The graphify example scripts scan source for drift, eager imports and routes, repair missing import edges into graph.json once, keep test code out of the pictures, and encode drift as one amber dash-patterned tint
description: `scripts/graphify/*` (template examples): bkit-graph-drift.py counts literal patterns over a product/tests partition with exact per-prefix budgets; bkit-graph-eager.py detects module-scope calls from source and counts downstream importers from graph.json; bkit-graph-surface.py joins routes to endpoints by literal scan with symbol-level attribution; bkit-graph-repair.py is the only writer of recovered import edges and runs before clustering on every graph-writing command; readers warn, never self-heal; bkit-graphify-rollup.py draws hue = called capability, dash + amber fill = any drift status, solid blue = budgeted, and keeps test code, eager findings and dead URLs off the diagrams.
rationale: External packages are not nodes in graph.json and graphify drops calls in module-level initialisers, so a duplicated mechanism or an import-time call is invisible to graph queries; a request URL is a string in a template literal, never an edge. Regex patterns like `new Ratelimit(` silently match nothing, which reads as clean. The test surface exists because test code is where guards live and a product-only scan cannot see inline `test()` statements; test helpers count as product because product-shaped code imports them. A surface walking zero files would pass every budget vacuously — the false green the script exists to prevent. Budgets downgrade a warning because one amber otherwise covers both an unbounded marker and a settled, CI-guarded count, and every sweep rediscovers the settled rows; an exact number with a reason and a two-way CI guard keeps it from hiding work. One repaired graph.json is the single source of truth so `graph:rollup` and `graphify affected` never disagree; a second on-read repair would need subtraction to keep two answers agreeing. Test-path rows are never painted because folder rollups smear one test row onto a whole package. One amber colour: no scan proves intent (a split can be deliberate, a bypass the one case the owner cannot serve, a dead URL a stub), so a ranked ramp would claim what the scans cannot support; dash patterns read in greyscale and for colourblind readers; emoji labels cannot be sized under GitHub's strict Mermaid. Budgeted rows still get a box because a budgeted bypass is still a bypass, and blue not green because green reads as `one`. Eager findings stay off the diagrams because hue and dash are already spoken for and the unit is per file, not per capability. The whole-repo graph.html (8.3 MB, ~9.8K nodes) renders as an unusable hairball. Mermaid edges under weight 12 are dropped because the module view is otherwise 322 edges. Reasons moved out of the script comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Graph-query drift detection — not adopted: cannot see external constructors. Brace-counting module scope — not adopted: template literals, regex and JSX unbalance it. Red/orange/yellow drift ramp — rejected: implies an unsupported ranking.

summary: Install/upgrade render choices in bkit-install.ts: gateway-keyed § Models, no opencode provider default, Codex agents emit no tools/sandbox_mode, self-bump re-execs the new binary, upgrade re-renders output and re-pins, check scopes to installed modules
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts`: § Models is keyed on gateway; effort ladders on program; an installed `.opencode/` with no recorded provider exits 1; Codex TOML agents carry no `tools:` or `sandbox_mode`; the opencode command anchor carries `$ARGUMENTS`; Cursor commands get the frontmatter description as their first line; `bkit upgrade --to/--latest` installs then re-execs; upgrade re-renders host agents/commands, `.bkit/*.md` docs and package.json gate scripts for installed hosts only and refreshes canonicalHashes + pinnedVersion unconditionally; `bkit check` resolves the opencode provider from the install and scopes drift to sentinel-detected modules; compliance grading resolves parentSha to a hex SHA.
rationale: Gateway keying stops § Models growing as programs x gateways, since a model id belongs to the gateway serving it. Rendering a provider-less opencode install against a substitute would silently rewrite every agent pin to a provider the consumer never chose; calling the resolver speculatively would fail consumers who never installed opencode. Falling back on an unknown effort program would emit a ladder the caller never chose. Codex has no per-agent tool allowlist (openai/codex#6049) and `sandbox_mode` would be `workspace-write` for every write-capable bkit agent, discriminating nothing, so the limitation is documented in providers.md instead of hidden behind a field that only looks restrictive. A stray triple-quote in a prompt would close the TOML value early. Without the `$ARGUMENTS` anchor the opencode command body replaced the user's input and lost the issue ref (#278). Dropping the Cursor description outright let the managed-version marker stand in as the description (#386). Re-exec matters because the running process is the OLD code, and rendering new templates with old logic is a correctness hole; coupling bump and re-render makes it impossible to strand a base branch's mirrors (#256). Without the upgrade re-render a version bump shipped new config but stale prompts/agents/docs; without the unconditional re-pin a clean upgrade left the pin stale and failed the CI drift gate (#129 §3). Without the installed-provider fallback an openrouter/opencode consumer reported false drift on check (#255 #8); without installed-module scoping a single-host repo reported the absent host's files as drift (#252). An unresolved parentSha made every diff-based rule grade an empty diff and pass vacuously, and collapsed compliance history into one identity; the earlier stats.jsonl scan for a workflow-started row could never match, so every row recorded HEAD~1. Upgrade renders opencode.json like install because the json deep-merge otherwise injected raw sentinel keys (#245). Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit-modules.ts mechanics: separate opencode/codex model lookups, .agents subtemplates from the template only, deferred version write, narrow settings prunes, opencode provider blocks replaced in existing order, Codex workflows as skills, cloud footprint opt-in
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts`: opencodeModelLookup and codexModelLookup are separate from the cursor modelLookup; `.agents/*.md` and `.bkit-version` never go through copyAdditive; the `.bkit/version` write waits for postDispatch; canonicalHashes drops paths bkit no longer keeps; the retired-ask-row prune is exact-string; the claude allow prune runs after the contained merge; opencode.json provider blocks are replaced (not merged) and rebuilt in the existing file's key order; `.claude/cloud.md` stays out of drift; opencode.yml provider drift is advisory only; Codex renders workflows as `.agents/skills/bkit-<wf>/SKILL.md` and writes no `.codex/config.toml`; deeper test tiers without a gate get an advisory, never a seeded stub.
rationale: Reshaping the shared cursor modelLookup would be a high-risk change touching every module signature for no functional gain. Copying `.agents/*.md` additively would dump bkit's own out-of-block content (its `### bkit Repo Authoring` section, friction-log entries) onto consumers, and race the templates pass, double-recording in dry-run; `.bkit-version` in the copy would pollute `.agents/` and break dry-run/install parity. Deferring the version write keeps a mid-install crash from suppressing the first-install banner on retry. A stale canonicalHashes key would keep exempting the file from checks such as the floating-tag check. The settings merge is additive and never prunes, so a row bkit stops shipping stays forever without an explicit prune; it is exact-string so a consumer's own ask rows are never touched, and runs from both engines because `bkit upgrade --latest` is the path the README points at. Pruning before the additive merge would re-seat the pruned row. Replacing provider blocks stops a hijacked npm/baseURL surviving reinstall (deepContains treats a corrupted superset as satisfied); template-first ordering made install and upgrade render different orders so `bkit check` never settled. cloud.md holds machine-local secret values, so drift there is expected. opencode.yml is self-installed and bkit does not own it; bkit-cloud.yml self-syncs on a provider switch via one fanned-out secret. Codex has no project-scoped command surface: custom prompts are user-level, deprecated for skills, and openai/codex#4734 / #9848 asking for `.codex/prompts` were closed NOT PLANNED; `.agents/skills` is on Codex's search path and already bkit's canonical directory, and cross-host visibility of those skills is accepted deliberately. Codex has one gateway because the ChatGPT subscription is what makes it cheap to run. A seeded gate stub for a deeper tier would exit 0 and claim coverage while the agent loop silently stops at static-unit. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Auto-rewrite opencode.yml — not adopted: file not bkit-owned. Pattern-based ask-row prune — rejected: would touch consumer rows.

summary: `bkit telemetry migrate` maps legacy status/severity/superseded by substring, keys on a truncation-safe slug, keeps friction workflow/step, skips each absent .md pair independently, treats a fresh repo as a clean no-op, and slugs `repo` from the git remote only
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-telemetry-migrate.ts`: legacy Status/superseded spellings map by substring; `partially-resolved` → OPEN; legacy severity `normal` and missing severity → MEDIUM; keys embed the legacy id and append a digest only on truncation; friction rows keep the legacy workflow/step; an absent `.md` skips only its pair; no legacy ledgers and no rows → nothing-to-migrate; issues.jsonl and completed.md count in the already-migrated / legacy-ledger checks; the bootstrap seed runs on every migrate; `repo` comes from the git remote, else `unknown/repo`.
rationale: An exact-equality status check silently defaulted prose like `RESOLVED — closed by …` to OPEN, marking closed work outstanding, and an exact superseded match reported real legacy spellings as ACTIVE; sharing the rule with the friction builder keeps the two from drifting. `normal` is the middle of a three-point scale; missing severity is an explicit unknown->neutral mapping to re-triage on next touch. Embedding the legacy id is safe because migration is a one-shot deterministic read, so two runs cannot race for a number. A 60-char truncated slug is not unique — titles diverging after char 60 collapse to one key and `fold()` keeps only the last, which hits recurrence entries hardest; short titles keep a readable key. Stripping the leading date from a heading would re-key the row so a re-migration mints new entities. Stamping `migrate` as workflow/step would put migrated friction rows on a different axis from live ones and blind the harvest's workflow/step slices. Gating idempotency on jsonl-non-empty aborted the whole run for any consumer missing one legacy pair. Without the fresh-repo check the run fell through to `abort(knowledge.md not found)` and printed `migrate failed` for a documented no-op. Without issues.jsonl in the rows-exist signal a completed.md-only consumer re-ran as nothing-to-migrate, and omitting completed.md from legacy ledgers stranded its rows. The bootstrap seed exists so the roadmap projection has rows for work already in flight on day one, and re-runs so FIDs added after the first migrate get seeded. package.json `name` differs from the slug by one character, and since `repo` is in identity() that forks every entity; a wrong-but-plausible slug forks silently while `unknown/repo` is visible. The one non-throwing JSONL parse primitive bounds the parse-miss class to one place instead of a log-and-continue catch per call site. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: Ledger schema choices in bkit-telemetry.ts: TRIAGED state, closed deferral reason enum with adjudicator-only `unjustified`, exhaustive deferral writer set, separate `subagent` and `step`, challenge-prompt severity vocabulary, cumulative failure count, `shippedAt`, scrubbed git env, numeric ts coercion
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-telemetry.ts`: triage ladder OPEN → TRIAGED → CLOSED; `reason` on deferrals is a closed enum (scope-declared / hard-blocked / needs-decision / own-cycle, plus adjudicator-only unjustified that later rows carry verbatim); DEFERRAL writer set excludes the plan executor and gaps-remediator; rows carry both `step` and `subagent`; severity reuses the challenge prompts' four levels; outcome rows carry a cumulative distinct-failure count; feature rows may carry a historic `shippedAt`; repo slug resolution scrubs hook git env vars; `ts` sorting coerces ISO strings; the telemetry summary compares against a rolling median.
rationale: Analysing and fixing are different events, often months apart: without TRIAGED a sweep that works out what an entry is must either lie with CLOSED or discard the analysis with OPEN, and collapsing them loses the interval. Before the reason enum, being declared was the only test for exemption and the agent wanting out of the work wrote its own declaration, so unfinished in-scope work looked identical to genuine out-of-scope work; a closed enum makes the claim testable, and a ledger row being the only place scope was ever declared is the tell. `unjustified` is never rewritten because the discipline rate measures how often an agent deferred work it should have done, not whether someone cleaned up after. The writer set is data because the prose contract alone did not hold: the executor wrote deferral rows despite an explicit NO out-of-scope deferral line, turning blocked in-scope work into something the build loop treats as settled. Conflating `step` and `subagent` costs the harvest a slice dimension and makes which-agent-causes-rework unanswerable. Sharing the challenge prompts' severity lets remediate pass it through without re-deriving. A per-run failure count would mark every run after the first-ever bug as an error run forever. `shippedAt` exists because append-time `ts` makes a backfilled historic ship sort as newest and evict genuinely recent ships. Hook-exported GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE make `git -C` answer for the hook's repo, so a harvest from a hook would stamp every consumer's rows with bkit's slug. `a.ts - b.ts` on a string ts is NaN, voiding the sort and making fold winners depend on file order. The median is outlier-robust and durations are right-skewed. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: `bkit:gate:*` names spell their tier chain; only static/unit/format/ship gates are seeded; deeper gates exist only when the consumer declares them; build stops at integration; ci.yml calls tool scripts directly
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts` BKIT_GATE_SCRIPTS: each gate chains its parent with tier names from the ci.yml job ids; the integration / e2e / live gates are never seeded; `/bkit-build` runs at most `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration`; `/bkit-debug` runs the deepest declared gate; husky templates run the same names; ci.yml does not; `lint:slop` is in no gate; detectGateAdvisories advises a repo that has a deeper tier but no gate for it.
rationale: Name and value describing the same sequence cannot disagree, a caller reads coverage off the name without opening package.json, and `scope` in status.jsonl is self-describing. Husky and agents running the same names means one edit changes both and they cannot drift. ci.yml needs per-step reporting, affected-package conditionals and tiers the local gate excludes, so it calls scripts directly. A seeded `pnpm test:integration` would hard-fail every repo without that tier, and an empty or stub value exits 0 so the workflow records a scope claiming coverage it never ran — the false-green #437 exists to kill; absence is load-bearing, which makes discoverability the problem the advisory solves. Build stops at integration because its diagnose → remediate loop can only repair what its own gate runs: a CI-only tier means build closes green, the PR reds and recovery needs a separate `/bkit-debug`; integration catches contract breaks the unit tier cannot at a cost the loop absorbs, while E2E (a production build plus a browser on every remediation attempt, minutes before CI runs the same on the PR) does not pay for itself. The static gate serves the plan-execute loop and the pre-push revert path, where the tree is knowingly inconsistent and the suite would fail on deletions it cannot fix. The Cursor GateGuard has no failClosed because an advisory hook that fails closed would block the edit it only meant to comment on. The Claude guardrails engine is never wired to a permissionDecision because that would turn an advisory into the blanket prompt the host removed; the Codex wiring text is separate because Cursor's wording names the wrong result and stdout shape and would wire a hook that silently never gates. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Seed deeper gates as stubs — rejected: false green. Run E2E in the build loop — not adopted: cost per remediation attempt.

summary: Phase-3 detectors: stale-render gates block only on main/dev (or PRs into them), fail safe when the branch is unknown, run after the Phase-2 re-stamp; managed-doc set comes from the package template tree; ci.yml drift is presence-only; @live/@smoke home check runs only where the convention is active
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts`: detectRenderedPromptsStale / detectManagedDocsStale are blockers on main/dev and advisories elsewhere; an undeterminable branch counts as protected; they run in Phase 3 so install/upgrade re-stamps first; managed docs are enumerated from `<templates>/docs`; the capstone drift check flags missing known-good fragments only and reads comment-stripped code; the tagged-test home check fires only when some package declares the script; owned-hook-missing fails check; alias collisions are advisory; Vercel installCommand and ci.yml token wiring are checked by raw regex; the BKIT_GH_TOKEN advisory is skipped in CI and without a github MCP server.
rationale: A stale render is almost never created by a feature branch; it is inherited from a dev where the package was bumped without an atomic re-render, so hard-failing every feature push for inherited drift was friction; main/dev stay hard blockers because stale doctrine must never land there, and the PR-into re-assertion keeps the skew from reaching a protected branch silently. An unknown branch must never silently downgrade the gate. Phase-3 placement avoids the chicken-and-egg where the gate would abort the install that fixes it. Globbing the consumer's docs/ would false-positive on every plan, since plans inherit the plan template's bkit:start block. ci.yml is freely edited, so a differs-from-canonical check would be all false positives, while a copy can silently lose a load-bearing invariant and reintroduce a fixed bug (the concurrency-cancel that killed a push-only @live canary); raw-text matching would pass any ci.yml seeded from the commented template. The tag check is convention-gated to stay silent on repos and incidental strings not using it; the capstone `live_ran > 0` assertion is the runtime backstop and this catches it earlier (#483 ghost-green). A deleted owned hook turns its guard off without a word because hook commands skip missing files. Alias collisions are pre-existing ledger data, not an install fault. The Vercel check closes the gap the #274 → 4.1.2 revert papered over (env var checked, installCommand never). A token advisory in CI would be log noise. The stub sentinel needs the full header form so prose back-references cannot fire an undismissable advisory. `bkit-decide` is invisible to the CI-Dispatch Gate, which then reports no-ci on every build and loses its ability to catch an undispatched run. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Hard-block stale renders on every branch — rejected: inherited drift friction.

summary: The Claude web setup script flips workspace trust and seeds `~/.claude/settings.json` autoMode with `//=`; cloud-bootstrap re-checks trust at the discovered root
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-cloud-env.ts` renders `@@CLOUD_WORKSPACE_TRUST@@` (merge-write `hasTrustDialogAccepted` for the baked repo path) and `@@CLOUD_USER_SETTINGS@@` (autoMode environment entries led by `$defaults`, seeded with `//=`). The registrable base of a provider baseURL is the naive last two labels. The egress fingerprint hashes derived bases and hosts only.
rationale: Allow rows grant capability, so Claude Code ignores them until trust is accepted, never shows the dialog in `claude -p`/SDK sessions, and announces it only on stderr — config that reads as configured and does nothing. The setup script is the only reliable place: cloud-bootstrap.sh is too late (settings resolve before SessionStart) and an in-session write cannot touch the protected `.claude/` path. The baked clone path is an observation, not a contract; baking plus discovery means a relocated clone costs one degraded session instead of a permanent silent no-op. The classifier deliberately ignores repo-level autoMode so a checked-in repo cannot inject its own allow rules, so bkit cannot ship it in-repo. Unconfigured, every context-fetch host is external, `Host containment` describes an open-internet machine (wrong behind an egress allowlist), and requests for the host's own credentials are blocked. `//=` never stomps a consumer's entries; the trade is that later bkit changes do not reach containers that already have them, the safer direction. Omitting `$defaults` discards every built-in trust slot. Base rewrites for public suffixes would silently widen or narrow a grant, while a registry-gate deny fails loudly. Hosts join the fingerprint because the Cursor paste is hosts-only. `apexBasesOf` stays a named export in bkit-cloud-env.ts because inlining it into integration-only bkit-modules.ts would erode the unit coverage floor. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Write trust from cloud-bootstrap.sh — rejected: too late. Ship autoMode in-repo — impossible: ignored by design.

summary: Each program is pinned to the gateway whose subscription is already paid; no gateway override. Uninstall strips settings arrays element-wise, deletes husks, clears the package.json `bkit` block, and upgrade keeps the drift hash on whole-file skips
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts` PROGRAM_GATEWAYS pins claude/cursor/codex to one gateway each; opencode names one. `.bkit/src/bkit-uninstall.ts` strips array entries element-wise, deletes a markdown file reduced to a lone heading or a residual equal to the stripped template, removes `.codex/agents/bkit-*.toml`, globs `.bkit/scripts/bkit-*`, and removes the `bkit` package.json object. `.bkit/src/bkit-upgrade.ts` resolves write strategy like install, never block-merges byte-equal-text, records a whole-file skip's hash only when disk equals template, and moves docs/warnings.md to docs/noise.md.
rationale: Pinning is policy, not capability: Cursor and OpenRouter can reach Claude models, but each program uses the subscription already paid for, and when one runs dry the escape is switching program, because the cheap gateway is attached to a different program. Whole-array uninstall equality left the WebFetch-enriched `allow` array behind while stripping `deny`/`ask`, leaving a repo strictly more permissive after uninstall. Lone-heading and template-equal residuals are bkit-authored husks (zero footprint). An extension-only filter would leave every Codex TOML agent behind. Globbing covers new scripts. Clearing the `bkit` object stops an uninstalled repo advertising prior choices. Install and upgrade must never disagree on a file and fight across runs; block-merging a byte-equal-text file would reformat it and churn forever against install. Recording a hash over consumer drift would erase the drift record (#459). Reseeding noise.md instead of moving it would strand every recorded downgrade in warnings.md. `--help` after a verb prints usage because users expect subcommand help. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Gateway override in Model Overrides — not adopted.

summary: Harvest prunes consumer friction only by byte-for-byte content after fsync + read-back, never clears or fold-rewrites the central store, keeps unparseable lines, and counts entities by fold
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-harvest.ts`: friction.jsonl is moved (copy → fsync → read back → prune by exact content), stats.jsonl copied; the store at repo-root `harvest/` accumulates every distinct row; malformed consumer lines are kept; deferral/failure counts fold same-key rows; the path-derived repo slug is a loud last resort.
rationale: An identity-gated prune was a real data-loss bug (#343): `fold()` collapses rows sharing an identity, and friction keys truncated to ~68 chars gave two distinct entries one identity, so the prune deleted colliding rows the store never kept. A store that kept only fold winners would drop rows an earlier run already pruned (winners change between runs), and clearing it would delete the originals' only copy on the next run. Pruning against in-memory rows would trust an unconfirmed write. Pruning a half-written tail would delete a row never stored; re-reading at prune time keeps rows appended mid-harvest; temp-file + rename avoids a torn ledger. Friction is a work queue that must drain; stats are the consumer's own history. Harvested data is neither managed nor shipped, so it lives outside `.bkit/`. A raw line count reports one deferral as two and inflates with every triage pass. The old last-two-path-segments slug made the owner a directory on the harvesting machine and minted a new identity per clone location. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Identity-gated prune — rejected: data loss.

summary: Analysis, status-hole and preflight signal rules: per-run failure delta, deferral discipline attribution, explicit MERGED-on-entry marker, orphan-step reporting, `web` context optional, context-fetch parser parity with the workflow awk, unnamed blocks exempt from provision pairing
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-analysis.ts` diffs cumulative failures per repo (clamped at 0) and computes the unjustified-deferral rate per (subagent, model) over folded entities; same-month rollups append-merge. `.bkit/src/bkit-status-hole-detector.ts` classifies MERGED_ON_ENTRY from the explicit marker, falling back to both worktree-setup and regression-guard absent, and reports orphan steps. `.bkit/src/bkit-preflight.ts` treats `web` as optional, parses markers like the bkit-debug awk, skips unnamed blocks for provision pairing, ignores comment lines in drift. `.bkit/src/bkit-registry.ts` is a pure-data leaf. `.bkit/src/bkit-tiers.ts` deep-merge follows template key order; markers wrapping the whole file trigger a one-time wholesale replace. `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts` treats a missing hash as consumer-modified.
rationale: Testing cumulative failures absolutely marks every run after the first bug as an error run, so the regression reads 100% error at every size; a falling total after a fold is not an error run. The discipline rate is attribution, not a leaderboard: a high rate means either a prompt under-specifying when deferring is legal or a turn budget running out (an agent near maxTurns defers instead of finishing), which need different fixes. Keying MERGED_ON_ENTRY on the absence of merge-pr / deferred-sweep would reclassify a double-hole Path A/B run and report zero holes — inferring the path from the evidence under audit hides the worst cases. Comparing heading vs literal steps is a tautology; an orphan step is a real prose bug no gate covers. A blocking hole gate on a 25–65% holey corpus is noise that gets disabled (384-tier3-promotion). Nagging every consumer for a third-party search key is noise; the host's web tools are the fallback. A marker the awk accepts but the parser rejects is a block that runs while every advisory reports it absent. An unnamed block can never pair with a provision block and would nag unfixably. Comments carry no load, so annotating a block must not trip drift. Registry branching lives in the coverage-measured bkit-cloud-env.ts; a leaf with imports could create cycles. Consumer key order once put `git push --force*: deny` after the force-with-lease allow, silently denying a permitted command (#255 P2-10). A hash comparison would eventually match any stable file, so whole-file-wrap detection is structural and self-limiting. Defaulting a missing hash to drift forces a conflict instead of a silent overwrite. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: Reasons behind `bkit <noun> <verb>` behaviours: signal-driven evidence clamp with a hard ceiling, roadmap without tracker issues, body-only skip-ci check, runtime probing limits, CI-dispatch lane-namespace match, protect-main binds admins and leaves dev open, exit 126/127 not a test failure, retired-path advisories, context-migrate marker swap and file deletion, alias-collision lint severities
description: `.bkit/src/commands/**` and helpers: `bkit context clamp` keeps signal lines plus head/tail under a 12000-line / 1.5 MB ceiling; `bkit roadmap fold` renders no tracker issues and ranks SHIPPED on shippedAt; the skip-ci body check ignores the subject; `bkit runtime` probes only gh auth and treats `CI=false` as not-CI; the CI-Dispatch probe matches the capstone's lane namespace; `bkit setup protect-main` binds admins and leaves dev unprotected; `bkit tests run` records exit 126/127 as never-ran; `bkit-retire` advises every consumer line calling a retired path; `bkit-context-migrate` swaps `debug-fetch:` markers and deletes `.agents/config.md`; `bkit-telemetry-lint` fails only on collisions and ignores `references[]`; normalise leaves unique numbered keys; `bkit-launch` execs the binary directly; locks refuse a feature split across month buckets; branch rebase union-resolves friction.jsonl.
rationale: Failure signal in local test output is flat or middle-weighted (102 consumer artifacts): head+tail kept as little as 10% of it, signal lines kept 100% while cutting 41–76% of bytes; the ceiling exists because signal immunity alone fails open exactly when things are worst, and over-matching only keeps more lines. A regenerated tracker list can only go stale and a wired tracker already shows the issues; a backfilled row would otherwise evict real recent ships. The defect is a squash body inheriting branch subjects' tokens, while subject `[skip ci]` is a docs-commit convention. gh auth is the flaky probe; `git push --dry-run` never fires a protected branch's hook, so a false true could strand a live session on dev; reading `CI=false` as ambiguous would cost a laptop its worktrees. One lane name breaks on rename and any-check counts Vercel/Renovate as CI. Agents act with the owner's admin token, so an admin exemption makes the agent the bypass; dev operators own that tests ran. Recording a never-ran gate as FAIL sends a debug loop chasing tests that never executed. Nothing else would tell a consumer a retired path call fails. A verbatim config.md move would leave markers nothing parses; matching only `context-fetch:` would strand `debug-fetch:` blocks forever; with no retired-file sweep, a leftover config.md would still read as authoritative. A legacy-seeded ledger pattern-teaches agents to keep minting numbered keys; minted keys only WARN because the one-shot migration legitimately produced them; counting references would invent collisions from cross-links; re-keying unique numbers would churn valid citations. `open -a` routes through launchd, which drops the inherited env (#279/#280). Either month bucket would be a guess. Union can resurrect a drained friction row, but the next harvest re-banks it while a blocking conflict halts the workflow. A slop-scan upgrade that drops a summary field would silently disable the gate; the failure text names the fixes agents reach for first because those make code worse while turning the gate green. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: Why specific bkit test guards exist: block-locality audit, frozen ship step keys, ctx-step bash extraction, whole-second ts gate, deferral reason/writer/unjustified gates on live ledgers, ungated workflow/step fields, telemetry spec-example validation, real-install provenance check
description: Test files under `.bkit/src/` assert: every `$VAR` in a workflow/prompt fence is assigned in that fence (bkit-block-locality-audit.test.ts, sources only); the 15 canonical `ship-*` keys never change (bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts); bkit-cloud.yml's ctx step runs as extracted bash against a stub gh (bkit-cloud-ctx-step.integration.test.ts); live ledgers carry no whole-second `ts` after the cutoff, deferral `reason` on the folded state, `unjustified` carried forward, only listed writers (bkit-ledger-integrity.test.ts); `.bkit/jsonl.md` examples pass the real codec (bkit-telemetry.test.ts); `.bkit/version` provenance survives a real install (bkit-install.integration.test.ts).
rationale: Shell state does not persist between Bash tool calls, so an unassigned `$VAR` expands empty and `jq --arg v "$X"` writes an empty field while exiting 0; it never fired (244 committed verdict rows carried values) only because the orchestrator substituted held values — correctness rested on undocumented model inference with nothing to detect when it stopped holding (#440). Auditing host mirrors would double-report and hold CI red until a re-install, turning a regenerable artifact into a merge blocker. Renaming a ship step key resets attempt counters across three repos and orphans the Tier-3 detector corpus. The ctx-step test exists because #363's plan called for bash-unit verification, none was committed, and build-challenge found H1 (FID truncation) and M1 (jq fail-open treating unparseable status.jsonl as zero rows, defeating the cap forever) only by manual dry-runs; extraction is by indentation because the repo ships no YAML parser. A hand-typed ts is round because a model reaches for `T00:00:00Z` and increments: stats.jsonl (shell idiom) was 0-for-63 whole-second while agent-appended ledgers were 44-for-270; pre-cutoff rows stay because re-minting history would invent data. `validate()` never sees `jq >>` appends, so the file is the only place to enforce the reason enum; `fold()` is last-write-wins, so the next append decides whether a reviewer's `unjustified` survives and the judged party is usually the appender. Backfilling `workflow` on manual rows would put invented data into analysis. Spec examples are what agents copy; `severity` and `references` were lost by examples drifting from the type. The provenance write path is a fresh object literal, so a field addition can silently drop it and a mocked install would never notice. Each workflow's own bash summary was wrong (`grep -c || echo 0` printing `0\n0`, jq `//` keeping empty strings, `wc -l` counting lines). Reasons moved out of test comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: Why further bkit test guards exist: archive subdirectory for superseded plans, template/repo action-pin parity, summary output-format verbs, closed-vocabulary backticks, one gate table per host family, single-emit and no-literal-list hook checks, preflight graded against the installed tracker, verdict vocabularies linked from files
description: Tests under `.bkit/src/`: superseded design/plan documents move into `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/archive/` (bkit-workflow-archive-snippet); repo and template workflows pin the same action SHAs (bkit-template-action-pins); summary prompts use one of three coverage verbs (bkit-summary-output-format); closed-vocabulary tokens are backticked outside fences (bkit-prompt-notation); every gate holds on every host (bkit-permissions-parity, bkit-gateguard-parity); preflight sees the tracker being installed (bkit-preflight-tracker-order); producer and consumer verdict vocabularies agree (bkit-verdict-vocabulary); this repo's .gitattributes carries a union rule for .bkit/friction.jsonl that the template does not (bkit-telemetry-gitattributes).
rationale: The close step once copied a fresh document over the canonical one, so re-running design or plan destroyed the previous document (#417); a rename in place would match the sub-plan and plan-presence globs in bkit-build.md / bkit-ship.md, while a subdirectory is invisible to every exact-name or non-recursive read; deriving the bucket with `date +%Y%m` broke a design crossing a month boundary (#416). Renovate ignores `.bkit/templates/**`, so template pins silently rotted until a consumer's CI broke; the snapshot pinned the stale value as expected. Summary prompts carried three unnamed contracts, and nothing separated do-not-drop-items from be-brief, so a summariser could drop rows; restating the rule twice on one line is how two statements drift apart. The predecessor notation rule (backtick only when compared) was undecidable and the corpus split 86% vs 68% bare for the identical construct; bracketed instructions inside fences were left behind in the first sweep. Per-host gate suites drifted (Cursor was missing gate-config, ALLOW_CONFIG_EDIT, deny-retry and docs-density cases). The install path resolved the tracker ~70 lines after preflight, so a linear → github switch told the consumer to add github but never to drop linear. bkit-ship.md gated DIAGNOSE_VERDICT as PASS|FAIL while dispatching the same agent other workflows gate as PASS|CONCERNS|FAIL, so a legitimate CONCERNS failed the ship gate; two verdict variables one edit apart let a typo silently read the wrong step's verdict. Union on friction.jsonl can resurrect rows harvest drained, so bkit does not impose it on consumers; this repo accepts the trade-off. A literal host list in a hook would drift unnoticed because nothing compares it to the registry; host-render mirrors are not drift-gated, so a template edited without re-install left the mirror stale. Asserting a test gate rather than the corpus stops a loosened checker looking like an honest pass. Reasons moved out of test comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Rename superseded documents in place — rejected: matches workflow globs.

summary: The Renovate example opens PRs against `dev` and layers `dev`'s config over `main`'s
description: `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5` sets `baseBranchPatterns: ["dev"]` and `useBaseBranchConfig: "merge"`. `useBaseBranchConfig` is itself read from the default branch, so it applies after one merge there.
rationale: bkit consumers gate `main` to PRs from `dev` only, so a PR Renovate opened against the default branch could not merge. Renovate reads its config only from the default branch; with `baseBranchPatterns: ["dev"]` and no `useBaseBranchConfig`, edits to `renovate.json5` on `dev` are invisible to Renovate and every config change would need a release to `main` before it took effect. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Renovate example batches updates weekly, opens CVE PRs immediately on `dev`, and caps open and hourly PRs
description: `schedule: ["before 6am on Monday"]`, `osvVulnerabilityAlerts: true`, `prConcurrentLimit: 10`, `prHourlyLimit: 4` in `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`.
rationale: A weekly batch keeps PR noise low. OSV alerts give the same effect as Dependabot's `automated-security-fixes`, but the PRs target `dev` through `baseBranchPatterns`, so bkit branch protection accepts them. The PR caps stop a flood of major-version bumps from swamping the repo. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Dependabot `automated-security-fixes` — not used: its PRs target the default branch, which accepts PRs from `dev` only.

references: docs/deployments.md § Renovate pnpm-11 freshness gate & microvm memory
summary: The Renovate example caps pnpm's worker pool in Renovate's runner and enforces release age in Renovate, with pnpm's own `minimumReleaseAge` set to 0
description: `env: { PNPM_WORKERS: "1", PNPM_MAX_WORKERS: "1" }` and `minimumReleaseAge: "1 day"` in `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`; consumers set `minimumReleaseAge: 0` in pnpm-workspace.yaml.
rationale: On a large pnpm-11 monorepo, `pnpm update --lockfile-only`, especially alongside a pnpm-level `minimumReleaseAge` gate that verifies publish timestamps for every lockfile entry, can exceed the physical memory of Mend's hosted microvm and fail with `kernel-out-of-memory` (a physical OOM, not a V8 heap limit), blocking every dependency PR; CI and Vercel pass because their runners have far more RAM (KN-CORE-10, KN-41). The worker cap is cheap and reversible and scoped to Renovate's runner, but may not clear a metadata-driven OOM on its own because `--lockfile-only` barely engages the worker pool. Enforcing release age in Renovate holds young dependencies out of PRs with no per-install timestamp check, removing the memory spike at the source and speeding every CI and Vercel build; security and OSV PRs bypass it, so CVE fixes are never delayed. pnpm 11 defaults the gate to 1440, so deleting the key leaves it active and drops the `@cbartens/*` exclusion, breaking same-day bkit upgrades; only 0 turns the per-entry check off. The trade-off is losing pnpm-level defence against fresh manual or transitive installs. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Renovate example lists `.bkit/templates/**` and `.agents/skills/**` in `ignorePaths`
description: Workflows copied out of `.bkit/templates/` stay out of `ignorePaths` so their action pins refresh.
rationale: Those trees are bkit-owned and rewritten by bkit; scanning them only produces onboarding noise. A packageRule `enabled: false` does not stop the github-actions manager scanning a file and applying `pinDigests`, so `ignorePaths` is the only way to keep Renovate off it. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Renovate example disables updates for `@cbartens/bkit`; bkit is upgraded with `pnpm bkit upgrade`
description: packageRule `{ matchPackageNames: ["@cbartens/bkit"], enabled: false }` in `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`.
rationale: `pnpm bkit upgrade --latest` bumps the pin and re-syncs bkit's files and `.bkit/templates/` in one step; a bare version bump skips the re-sync and leaves the consumer split-brain. The package lives on GitHub Packages (restricted), which Mend's hosted runner has no token for, so Renovate would only ever log a "no-result" lookup. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Renovate example carries a commented `hostRules` read token for npm.pkg.github.com; Mend uses a repository secret, self-hosted uses the workflow's RENOVATE_HOST_RULES
description: `hostRules` with `token: "{{ secrets.BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL }}"` is commented out in `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`.
rationale: Renovate resolves the whole workspace to regenerate the lockfile; without a read token for npm.pkg.github.com the regeneration 401s and CI then fails `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. The block stays commented so the self-hosted workflow's env auth is not doubled. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Renovate example puts every auto-mergeable non-major npm bump in one PR and gives each multi-package ecosystem one lockstep PR for majors only
description: Dev minor/patch, prod patch, `@types/**` and the eslint family share `groupName: "non-major dependencies"`; `@types/**` and eslint rules are scoped to minor/patch; `@tanstack/**`, `vitest*`/`@vitest/**` and `@playwright/**` have major-only groups.
rationale: Every Renovate PR rewrites pnpm-lock.yaml, so several PRs firing in the same window force serial rebases and stall `platformAutomerge`; one shared group means one weekly lockfile change, one merge, no rebase cascade. The `@types` and eslint pattern rules carry no update-type filter otherwise, so without the minor/patch scope a major bump would join the auto-merge group instead of falling to the majors rule. A coordinated breaking bump (e.g. `@tanstack/react-query` + `@tanstack/query-core`) must land together; without the major-scoped group each package would get its own PR and the halves would fail CI against each other. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Renovate example never auto-merges prod minor bumps, majors, GitHub Actions or Docker base images, and sets `automerge: false` explicitly
description: Explicit `automerge: false` on the prod-minor, majors, github-actions and dockerfile rules in `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`.
rationale: Minor prod bumps ship new behaviour to users; a major bump needs a human to read the changelog; a workflow action bump can change CI behaviour; a base-image bump can shift the build toolchain. `false` is written out, not left absent, so the policy is greppable and an earlier matching automerge rule cannot silently flip it to true. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

references: docs/deployments.md § Renovate — fencing bkit's own footprint
summary: bkit's own Renovate config does not bump vite majors; vite stays on ^6 via root `pnpm.overrides`
description: `{ matchPackageNames: ["vite"], matchUpdateTypes: ["major"], enabled: false }` in `.github/renovate.json5` (bkit repo only); `package.json` `pnpm.overrides.vite` is `^6.4.2`.
rationale: vite 8 switched its default transformer to oxc, which fails transforming the bkit integration tests. Lift the hold when vitest supports vite 8. Reasons moved out of `.github/renovate.json5` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own Renovate config does not bump pnpm majors
description: `{ matchPackageNames: ["pnpm"], matchUpdateTypes: ["major"], enabled: false }` in `.github/renovate.json5` (bkit repo only); `packageManager` is pnpm 10.
rationale: pnpm 11 is a config migration, not a drop-in bump: it ignores `pnpm.overrides` in package.json (they must move to pnpm-workspace.yaml) and blocks esbuild's build script by default (needs `onlyBuiltDependencies`), so it lands as a deliberate change, not a Renovate PR. Reasons moved out of `.github/renovate.json5` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Linear → GitHub importer takes `GH_PROJECT_TOKEN`, then the keyring token (`gh auth token --secure-storage`), then plain `gh auth token`
description: `resolveGhToken` in `scripts/linear/linear-to-github-import.ts` (bkit repo only).
rationale: The keyring token typically has `project` scope; plain `gh auth token` may return an env-loaded fine-grained PAT that lacks it, and Projects v2 writes then fail. Reasons moved out of the script's comments and README (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Linear → GitHub importer does not port the Linear project label (`cbartens/bkit`)
description: `LABEL_SKIPLIST` in `scripts/linear/linear-to-github-import.ts` (bkit repo only).
rationale: Linear models the project as a label; on GitHub the Projects v2 board already records the project, so the label would be redundant. Reasons moved out of the script's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI honours `[skip ci]` / `[skip actions]` only from a push commit message, never from a PR title
description: `Read Markers` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (bkit repo only) feeds `SKIP_MSG` only when `EVENT_NAME` is `push`; a pull_request title is read for force markers but never for skip markers.
rationale: A PR-title skip would turn off `bkit-tests-check`, bkit's sole required branch-protection check, so a PR could reach a merge with no suite run. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI recognises `[force full]` and maps it to run_level=full, the same as `[force build]`
description: `Read Markers` and `Decide Run Level` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (bkit repo only) accept `[force full]`; it yields `run_level=full` with `source=marker:force-full`. In the consumer scaffold it additionally bypasses `web_affected` (integration + e2e + @live).
rationale: bkit is one package with no deploy and no affected-graph, so `[force full]` has nothing extra to bypass here; it is recognised only so the consumer-scaffold marker is exercised in bkit's own CI. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI warns on dev pushes when the default branch serves stale Renovate config or workflows
description: `Check Default Branch Lags Dev` in `bkit-tests-static` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, bkit repo only) diffs `.github/renovate.json5`, `.github/renovate.json` and `.github/workflows` between `origin/<default>` and HEAD on dev pushes and writes a run-summary block + `::warning::`; it never fails. It mirrors the consumer scaffold's `main-lag-warning` block without the stub markers.
rationale: CI on dev proves the code, but nothing else checks that the code reached the default branch, and Renovate config plus scheduled / default-branch Actions are read live from the default branch. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's CI static lane and the cloud claude job install a pinned, checksum-verified vale tarball
description: `Install Vale` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (vale 3.9.1, sha256-checked, then `vale sync` with three attempts) and `Install vale` in the claude job of `.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml` / `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml` (same version and checksum).
rationale: vale is not on GitHub's runner image and `.vale/styles/` is gitignored, so without an explicit install `lint:prose` soft-skips (see `f9-lint-prose-restores-vale-styles-soft-skips-only-missing-binary`) and the prose gate is silently off in CI; in the cloud job, cloud-bootstrap.sh's `vale sync` and the dispatched phase's lint:prose would also no-op, unlike the cloud.md web env whose setup script installs vale. Reasons moved out of `ci.yml` and `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI cancels superseded runs only on pull_request, never on push to main/dev
description: `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (bkit repo only) is `${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`; push runs key on `github.run_id`.
rationale: Release and main/dev CI runs are observed by downstream `workflow_run` triggers, which must see them complete rather than cancelled. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI validates `.github/workflows/*` with actionlint
description: `Run actionlint` in `bkit-tests-static` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, bkit repo only) downloads actionlint 1.7.12 through a SHA-pinned installer script and runs it over the workflows.
rationale: A YAML linter accepts workflows that are valid YAML but invalid GitHub Actions; actionlint checks `${{ }}` expression syntax and runs shellcheck on `run:` blocks, catching that class. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI runs the Tier-3 status-hole detector on every static lane, fail-open
description: `Check Status Holes` in `bkit-tests-static` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, bkit repo only) runs `pnpm bkit:audit:status || true`; the CLI exits 0 even when it finds holes.
rationale: `384-tier3-promotion` promotes the detector to a blocking gate only after one release of fail-open signal without muting, and that signal accrues only if something runs it. `|| true` is a second guard; the CLI's own contract is exit 0 always. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The unit coverage gate lives in one package.json script that both bkit's CI unit lane and /bkit-build Run Tests run
description: `test:coverage:unit` in `package.json` carries `--coverage.include` and `--coverage.thresholds.branches`; `Run Unit Tests` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the /bkit-build Run Tests step (via `bkit:gate:static-unit`) both call it; the CI step only appends the JSON reporter + outputFile for the executed-count.
rationale: A coverage drop then fails in the build worktree before CI sees it, and bumping the threshold in package.json moves both callers together. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's unit coverage is scoped by an explicit `--coverage.include` list passed on the CLI; the bkit-modules data registry is outside it
description: `--coverage.include` in the `test:coverage:unit` script (`package.json`) names `.bkit/src/bkit-{analysis,cli,...,wording}.ts` plus `.bkit/src/commands/**/*.ts`; `bkit-modules`, `bkit-registry`, `bkit-context-migrate`, `bkit-status-hole-detector` and `bkit-telemetry-migrate` are not listed. The branch floor `--coverage.thresholds.branches=70` sits just below current and is ratcheted up.
rationale: The bkit-modules data registry is exercised end-to-end by integration tests, not unit-tested. vitest coverage is per run, not per project, so the scope has to be a CLI flag on the run. No reason is recorded for leaving out the other four files. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI runs unit and integration tests as separate parallel jobs, each with its own coverage number and executed-count
