description: `bkit-tests-unit` and `bkit-tests-integration` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (bkit repo only) are parallel siblings of `bkit-tests-static`; each emits `tests_ran`, and `bkit-tests-check` asserts each lane executed >0 tests. e2e / migrate / live lanes exist only in the consumer template.
rationale: Separate lanes give each tier its own honest coverage number and executed-count, mirror how consumers (consumer-a, consumer-b) run their tiers, and exercise the per-tier `bkit-stub:coverage` scaffold shipped to consumers. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's integration coverage is report-only and scoped to the engine surface; the lane is gated on execution, not a percentage
description: `Run Integration Tests` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (bkit repo only) passes `--coverage.include='.bkit/src/bkit-{modules,install,upgrade,uninstall}.ts'` and no `--coverage.thresholds`; `bkit-tests-check` requires `integration_ran > 0`.
rationale: A hard integration percentage punishes the correct test-pyramid shape (testing.md § Coverage on PRs). Scoping to the engine surface makes the number reflect the flows integration tests are meant to drive, not a whole-repo denominator. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit-cloud.yml keys concurrency per trigger surface; dispatch and the auto-ship it triggers never share a group
description: `concurrency.group` in `bkit-cloud.yml` is `bkit-auto-${{ inputs.issue || github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}`; races between a dispatched build and its auto-ship are handled by the orchestrator stale-run guard + status.json lock.
rationale: GitHub evaluates `concurrency.group` from trigger-payload context only, before any step runs. The dispatch payload exposes only the bare issue number; the workflow_run payload exposes only `head_branch` (`feat/{FID-with-slug}`). GHA expressions have no regex / split / replace-to-numeric, so stripping `feat/` yields `141-cloud-app`, not `141`, and the two tokens cannot be made identical. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: `bkit_dev_dispatch_guard` picks the FID's status directory with a sorted `find`
description: `status_dir=$(find docs/plans ... -path "docs/plans/*/logs/$guard_fid" | sort | head -1)` in both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: An unsorted `find` takes readdir order, so a FID whose logs span two YYYYMM buckets could read the cap counter from one file and write it to another across cycles, silently unbounding the cap. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: `bkit_dev_dispatch_guard` refuses to dispatch when the FID's status.jsonl cannot be parsed; only an absent file counts as zero
description: In both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml`, a failing `jq -s` over the status file returns 1 with `::notice::... is unparseable — refusing to dispatch ... uncounted (fail-closed)`.
rationale: A truncated line, stray non-JSON row or merge=union conflict artefact must not degrade to `dev_count=0`, which would defeat the cap entirely. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The dev-dispatch landing check wraps `git show` in its own `|| true` before piping to jq
description: `landed=$( (git show "origin/dev:${status_file}" 2>/dev/null || true) | jq -s ... || echo 0)` in both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: Under pipefail, a failing `git show` (row never landed) plus a succeeding jq that prints `0` makes the pipeline fail, firing `|| echo 0` a second time; `$landed` becomes a two-line value that breaks the `-lt` comparison and bypasses the fail-closed check. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The dev arm's commit-scope FID regex accepts both GitHub (`363-slug`) and Linear (`bar-123-slug`) shapes
description: `grep -oE '^\w+\((([0-9]+|[a-z]+-[0-9]+)-[a-z0-9-]+)\):'` in both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml`, the same alternation as the feat/** fallback. The kill switch (`gh issue view`) is GitHub-Issues-only, so a Linear FID no-ops there.
rationale: Kept for forward-compatibility with a future MCP-based kill switch, not as a present end-to-end guarantee: the workflow's kill switch and permissions are GitHub-Issues-only, so the dev trigger does not work for Linear-tracker consumers today. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The dev arm's linked-PR FID fallback reads only same-repo MERGED PRs, matching the repo via `env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY` inside `--jq`
description: `gh api repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/pulls --jq '[.[] | select(.head.repo.full_name == env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY and .merged_at != null)] | .[0].body // empty'` in both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: The endpoint returns PRs associated with the commit, which for a dev commit includes OPEN fork PRs branched at that SHA; the job-level `head_repository` guard gates the trigger, not this lookup, so an unfiltered `.[0]` would let an outsider's PR body choose the FID this trusted job dispatches against. The legitimate feature PR is merged and same-repo by construction. The repo name is read through `env.` because `gh api` has no `--arg`, and splicing it into the filter text would be injectable. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit-cloud.yml's kill switch matches the `bkit:auto` label exactly (`grep -qxF`), never as a substring
description: Every `gh issue view "$ISSUE" --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' | grep -qxF 'bkit:auto'` check in both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: A substring `grep -q 'bkit:auto'` over the label list also matches `bkit:auto-disabled`, `bkit:auto-paused` or `no-bkit:auto`, defeating the kill switch for an operator who believes such a label revokes automation. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: On the dev arm, the bkit:auto kill switch runs before the stale-run guard and the dispatch-cap guard
description: In both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml`, the `gh issue view ... grep -qxF 'bkit:auto'` check precedes `LATEST_CI_SHA` / the stale-run guard and `bkit_dev_dispatch_guard`; it needs nothing they set.
rationale: `bkit_dev_dispatch_guard` mkdir -p's, commits and pushes a telemetry row to dev; in the reverse order, an operator who removed bkit:auto to halt a misbehaving loop would still get bkit-auto[bot] commits pushed to dev on every later red dev CI. The removed comment named the stale-run guard as the writer; that guard now writes only to the run summary. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The dev stale-run guard selects the CI workflow by filename (`--workflow ci.yml`), not by its display name
description: `gh run list --branch dev --workflow ci.yml --status completed` in both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: The display name (`CI`) is consumer-editable free text; the filename is fixed. The removed comment said `bkit install` fixes the filename; install no longer writes ci.yml, and the fixed name is now the copy target in `.bkit/templates.md` § Contract. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: When the dev stale-run guard finds no completed CI run, it proceeds and emits a `::warning::` naming the ci.yml filename requirement
description: `if [ -z "$LATEST_CI_SHA" ]` in both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml` writes `::warning::gh run list --branch dev --workflow ci.yml returned no completed runs — stale-run guard disabled ...`.
rationale: Fail-open is recorded in `363-dev-stale-run-guard-by-ci-recency`; a PERMANENT misconfiguration (the consumer's CI workflow file is not literally ci.yml) looks the same as a transient API failure unless flagged, so the warning stops the guard running disabled for months unnoticed. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The feat/** branch-name fallback keeps the FULL FID slug; ISSUE is derived from it
description: `FID=$(echo "$BRANCH" | sed -E 's#^feat/##')` in both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml`; ISSUE (short numeric/alpha prefix, used only for `gh issue view`) is derived from the full FID.
rationale: A truncated FID (e.g. `363` instead of `363-widen-bkit-cloud-trigger`) would count against a different status.jsonl / status_dir key than the dev-path FID, breaking the one-shared-budget-per-FID invariant and orphaning a `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{truncated}/` directory. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The feat/** arm no-ops while a build is still running on the branch
description: In both jobs of `bkit-cloud.yml`, if the branch's status.jsonl shows a build `workflow-started` with no later `workflow-done` / `workflow-failed` and its newest build row is under 1800 s old, the ctx step exits with `skip=true`; unreadable status fails open.
rationale: Dispatching debug or ship then would put a second agent on the same branch mid-run. Build pushes before opening its PR, so this fires only when a PR from an earlier attempt is still open. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The opencode job installs opencode with a pinned `--version`
description: `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash -s -- --version 1.17.13` in `Install opencode` of `bkit-cloud.yml`; no updater bumps it.
rationale: A bare `| bash` installs whatever opencode.ai/install resolves as latest at run time: unpinned remote code executing with the runner token. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The self-hosted Renovate example serialises runs and queues rather than cancels
description: `concurrency: { group: renovate, cancel-in-progress: false }` in `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/renovate.yml` and `.github/workflows/renovate.yml`.
rationale: Two overlapping Renovate processes race on the same renovate/* branches and the Dependency Dashboard issue. Cancelling mid-push can leave a half-written branch or PR, and Renovate is idempotent, so a queued run that supersedes an identical pending one is harmless. Reasons moved out of the renovate.yml example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The self-hosted Renovate example wakes daily at an off-hour minute, never Monday-only
description: `cron: "17 6 * * *"` in `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/renovate.yml` and `.github/workflows/renovate.yml`; Renovate's own `schedule` in renovate.json5 gates normal update PRs.
rationale: osvVulnerabilityAlerts CVE PRs bypass Renovate's internal schedule and must be able to open on the next daily wake, not once a week. The off-hour minute avoids top-of-hour congestion, and each wake is a fast no-op when nothing is due (Renovate exits in seconds outside its window). Reasons moved out of the renovate.yml example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The self-hosted Renovate example allow-lists `PNPM_*` so the shared renovate.json5 `env:` block is accepted
description: `RENOVATE_ALLOWED_ENV: "PNPM_*"` in `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/renovate.yml` and `.github/workflows/renovate.yml`; renovate.json5 ships `env: { PNPM_WORKERS, PNPM_MAX_WORKERS }` for both runners.
rationale: renovate.json5 is one config shared by Mend and the self-hosted runner, so the worker-cap env stays in it even though the OOM it mitigates cannot happen on a 16 GB runner; without the allow-list the self-hosted bot rejects the whole config. Reasons moved out of the renovate.yml example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit owns only what a workflow step runs or parses; every shipped file is an owned file, an owned part of a shared file, or a template
description: **Owned file** — install and upgrade overwrite it; uninstall removes it while it still matches its `.bkit/version` hash: workflow, prompt, agent and command copies, `docs/templates/bkit-plan.md` and `docs/templates/bkit-audit-*.md`, `.bkit/.env.example`, `.bkit/scripts/bkit-slop-type-suppression.mjs`, and the hook scripts (`.claude/hooks/*`, `.codex/hooks/*`, `.cursor/hooks/*`, `.opencode/plugin/gateguard.js`). **Owned part of a shared file** — bkit rewrites and removes only its part: markdown between `bkit:start` and `bkit:end` (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/rules.md`, `.agents/docs.md`, `.agents/context.md`, `.agents/skills.md`, `.bkit/prompts.md`, `docs/*.md`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`); hook entries and permissions in `.claude/settings.json`; Cursor and Codex `hooks.json`; `permission`, `plugin`, `mcp` and `provider` in `.opencode/opencode.json`; the tracker entry under `mcpServers` in `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`. The `bkit:gate:*` / `bkit:deps:*` names in `package.json` are added when missing and never rewritten. **Template** — never applied to the repo; raw copies refresh in the consumer's `.bkit/templates/` (`isTemplate`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts`), including one context-fetch file per provider under `.bkit/templates/context/`. No file is written once and then hash-tracked: bkit either keeps a file current or leaves it to the consumer. Every owned file and owned block that is not JSON carries the managed-version marker (`489-managed-version-marker-on-every-written-file`).
rationale: A file a workflow step runs or parses has to match the workflows, so bkit keeps it current; a file a person or another tool runs belongs to the consumer's stack, so it ships as a template (issue body). The managed block of `.agents/context.md` holds the marker formats, self-skip contract and `allowed-domains` / `mcp-servers` rules that `/bkit-debug` and install parse, so bkit keeps it current; the ready-made fetch blocks are templates (`489-context-fetch-blocks-are-per-provider-templates`). The write-once, hash, upgrade-conflict and uninstall-reclaim machinery existed only so bkit could claim a consumer's file still matched the installed version; once the consumer decides whether to adopt, that claim is gone (issue body). Hooks stay owned because they enforce what workflows and prompts forbid (force push, `--no-verify`, `git reset --hard`) and change in step with them, so a stale copy runs workflows under old guards with no signal. The JSON keys stay owned because install fills them from install choices (`@@OPENCODE_TRACKER_MCP@@`, `@@OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY@@`), the tracker MCP entry is what tracker steps write through, and these files change often (settled plan 2026-10-07 §1). Accepted cost: bkit no longer promises that a consumer's CI, hooks and prose-lint config match the installed version, so workflows must not call those files (`467-workflows-reach-templates-only-via-commands-and-package-json-settings`).
alternatives: The issue body's boundary table, with MCP config and the gate scripts on the template side — rejected in the 2026-10-07 settled plan as too coarse: tracker steps need the tracker MCP entry, workflows run the gate scripts, and the table missed that workflows still called some template files (those calls were removed first, in #467). `.agents/context.md` as create-if-missing (Wave 2a, ef1f09a7) — reversed 2026-10-10 (owner, #489 "Decided (2026-10-10)"): its managed rules would freeze at the version first installed while the code that reads the blocks keeps changing.

summary: Ready-made context-fetch blocks ship as one template per provider in `.bkit/templates/context/`; the managed block of `.agents/context.md` holds only the rules
description: `.bkit/templates/context/` holds one file per provider: `github` (`context=ci` and `context=diff`), `expo` (`context=runtime` and `context=e2e`), `maestro` (`context=e2e`, every failed job matching `MAESTRO_JOB_RE`, iOS and Android lanes), `playwright`, `tavily`, `sentry`, `vercel`, `supabase`, `stripe`, `resend`, `inngest`, `cloudrun`, `serena`. Each file holds that provider's fetch blocks, its `context-fetch:provision` block where a stack CLI is needed, its env vars, the `allowed-domains` lines bkit's egress registry does not already derive, and its `mcp-servers` names. Project names, slugs and ids are placeholders (`your-team-slug`, `your-project-ref`, …) on a commented assignment line or env default, never a consumer's names (`.bkit/templates.md:76-92`, `.bkit/src/bkit-context-templates.test.ts:118`). `isTemplate` copies them raw into the consumer's `.bkit/templates/context/` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:307-308`). The managed block of `.agents/context.md` keeps only the rules — marker formats, contexts, self-skip contract, output bounds, provisioning, `allowed-domains` and `mcp-servers` — and bkit keeps it current. A consumer copies a provider's blocks below `<!-- bkit:end -->` and adds its domains and MCP names to their lists (`.bkit/templates.md:52-102`). The `context-fetch-source-not-enabled` advisory reads block names from these templates and names the file to copy (`shippedContextFetchTemplates`, `.bkit/src/bkit-preflight.ts`).
rationale: The managed half of `.agents/context.md` is the rules `/bkit-debug` and install parse; freezing it at first install leaves agents acting on stale rules while the code that reads the blocks moves on, so it stays bkit-owned and current. Examples are not rules, so they are templates the consumer adopts and owns. One file per provider, never one per block or per platform (owner 2026-10-10), because the domains and MCP server names a block needs belong with that block. Folder `.bkit/templates/context/` is the owner's choice over the proposed `context-fetch/` (#489 "Decided (2026-10-10)"). Placeholders keep any one consumer's names out of shipped files (#489 proposal 2026-10-10).
alternatives: (1) `.agents/context.md` create-if-missing, examples kept inside its managed block (Wave 2a, ef1f09a7) — rejected: the rules freeze at the version first installed. (2) Separate allowed-domains and MCP-server templates — rejected: the hosts and servers a block needs belong with that block. (3) Folder `.bkit/templates/context-fetch/` — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10); no reason recorded.

summary: Every file and block bkit writes or refreshes carries the managed-version marker, except JSON
description: One marker text (`bkit:managed vX.Y.Z — do NOT edit; run `bkit upgrade` to refresh`) in the file's comment syntax: `<!-- … -->` in markdown, `# <!-- … -->` in shell, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.env.example` and codex TOML agents, `// …` in JS hooks and `.mjs` scripts. In a markered file it is the first line inside the bkit block; in a whole file it sits below the first heading or frontmatter, or on line 2. Sources carry `{{BKIT_MANAGED_MARKER}}`; the comment prefix in front of the token picks the form (`applyTokens`, `.bkit/src/bkit-tokens.ts`; `managedVersionMarker`, `readManagedVersion`, `.bkit/src/bkit-version.ts`). Rendered prompts, agents, commands and skills are stamped at render. JSON files where bkit owns keys carry none. `detectManagedStale` (`bkit-managed-stale`, `.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts`) checks every stamped file: blocker on main/dev, advisory on feature branches.
rationale: A consumer who bumps the bkit package without re-rendering leaves agents reading stale rules and hooks; the marker lets `bkit check` catch that on every file bkit writes, not only docs and prompts. JSON has no comment syntax. Accepted cost: every release changes every managed file in the consumer's diff.

summary: The set of files checked for a stale marker is derived from what install writes, and a test asserts every written file carries one
description: `listStampedFiles(cwd)` (`.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts`) joins the core templates install writes, every manifest entry that is neither JSON nor generated, and the rendered agents, commands and skills on disk. `bkit-upgrade.integration.test.ts` installs every host into a fresh repo, asserts every tracked non-JSON, non-template file carries the marker at the installing version and that the set equals `listStampedFiles`, then rewinds every marker and checks `check` flags them and `upgrade` restamps them with no conflicts. A real install exits 1 when a written file lacks a marker.
rationale: A hand-kept list misses new file types; a derived set plus a test that fails on any unstamped file keeps the next one from shipping without a marker.

summary: bkit's own `.bkit/*.md` sources carry the literal `{{BKIT_MANAGED_MARKER}}` line; installing into this repo skips them
description: `.bkit/{cloud,jsonl,providers,templates,trackers,workflows,README}.md` and `.bkit/prompts.md` in this repo are the package sources and hold the token, never a version. `runBkitDocs` skips a doc whose source and destination are the same file.
rationale: A version stamped into a package source would be rewritten on every release and shipped as a hardcoded value.

summary: Templates carry no `bkit:start` / `bkit:end` blocks; only files bkit writes do
description: `ci.yml`, `bkit-cloud.yml`, `.vale.ini`, `.vale/styles/House/*.yml`, `.prettierignore` and `.cursor/Dockerfile` under `.bkit/templates/` hold plain content. The ci.yml advisories `ci-yml-missing-actionlint` and `ci-yml-run-injection` recognise an adopted ci.yml by an uncommented `bkit-tests` or `bkit-tests-<lane>` job (`ADOPTED_CI_JOB_RE`); `ci-yml-capstone-contract-drift` keys on the `bkit-tests-check` job.
rationale: bkit never writes a template, so a block in one signals ownership bkit does not have.

summary: `.agents/skills.md` is a managed block like `.agents/context.md`; the create-if-missing group is deleted
description: Install and upgrade refresh the block between `<!-- bkit:start -->` and `<!-- bkit:end -->`; content below `bkit:end` (`Project Skills`) is the consumer's; uninstall strips only the block; `bkit check` flags a stale block. `CREATE_IF_MISSING_PATHS` and `writeIfAbsent` are deleted. `bkit skills prune` reads the whole file.
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: the universal skills table stays current. Accepted cost: a consumer who edited inside the block loses those edits on the first upgrade, and one who removed the markers gets a fresh block appended.

summary: bkit's own CI cancels superseded runs only on pull_request, never on push to main/dev
description: `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (bkit repo only) is `${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`; push runs key on `github.run_id`.
rationale: Release and main/dev CI runs are observed by downstream `workflow_run` triggers, which must see them complete rather than cancelled. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI keeps one run per branch or pull request, as the template does
description: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` concurrency: group `ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.pull_request.number) || github.ref }}`, `cancel-in-progress: true`, same as `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: bkit uses its own templates completely. A push plans from the last green run on the branch, so a cancelled run's changes stay in scope of the run that replaced it; `bkit-cloud.yml` routes only success/failure conclusions, so a cancelled run is simply not routed. bkit's `ci-yml-capstone-contract-drift` advisory already asked consumers for this shape.

summary: Every template bkit ships is adopted in this repo verbatim or with a listed set of edits, and a test enforces it
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-dogfood-templates.test.ts` holds one entry per template: identical, adopted with an ordered list of labelled edits (`placeholder` / `adapt` / `bkit-only`), not adopted (`.github/dependabot.yml`: this repo uses Renovate), or generated (`docs/capabilities.md`). The repo copy must equal the template after the listed edits, byte for byte. `ci.yml` is the template with the planner, integration and capstone lanes enabled and three bkit-only steps (`Assert Dist Freshness`, `Check Status Holes`, bats). `package.json` carries no inline `lint-staged` key, so `.lintstagedrc.json` is the config lint-staged loads.
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: "we need to COMPLETELY eat our own dogfood". A template improvement found here goes into the template so consumers get it; a difference with no label fails the test.

summary: In the template ci.yml, `[force build]` and `[force cache]` make a lane run even when the same commit already passed
description: The `Check SHA Cache` step in `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/ci.yml` skips a lane when the commit passed CI in the last 7 days, unless the commit message or PR title carries `[force build]` or `[force cache]`.
rationale: Without it a re-push of an already-green commit skipped every lane and `[force cache]` did nothing; bkit's own CI already behaved this way.

summary: The template slop-scan config exempts test files from `tests.duplicate-mock-setup` only
description: `.bkit/templates/slop-scan.config.json` scopes its test-file override to `tests.duplicate-mock-setup`; type-escape casts and duplicate signatures in tests are findings like anywhere else, and `slop:delta` fails only on new ones. The shipped `guardrails.cjs` hooks carry a per-file opt-out.
rationale: `.agents/rules.md` "fix code, not gates": exemptions are per file with a reason, never a whole category. bkit's own config already ran this way.

summary: bkit's own pnpm overrides and allowed build scripts live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
rationale: pnpm 11 ignores `pnpm.overrides` in `package.json` and blocks esbuild's build script unless allowed. Reason moved out of config comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own renovate.json5 holds vite and pnpm major updates
rationale: vite is held at ^6 through pnpm overrides; pnpm majors change lockfile and config behaviour and are adopted by hand. Reason moved out of config comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own graphify rollup uses `MMD_MIN_WEIGHT=6`
rationale: At 6 the capabilities diagram draws 21 files and 32 links; 12 drops it to 11 files. Reason moved out of the script comment (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Cursor gateguard hook is byte-identical to Claude's
rationale: One advisory engine, two drivers; parity tests hold them equal. Reason moved out of the slop-scan config comment (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The `guardrails.cjs` hooks' empty catches are their fail-open contract
rationale: A hook that throws blocks the agent's tool call; guardrails return no opinion on any internal error instead. Reason moved out of the slop-scan config comment (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit carries no code, flag, command or setting without a production caller
description: Removed 2026-10-10: named managed blocks and the `optional` block flag (`extractNamedBlocks`); the `bkit codex` verb (no handler); `--keep-npmrc`; `bkit prs guard-checkout`; `bkit branches rebase --onto/--abort`; `bkit runs dispatch --retrigger-suffix` and its `autoroute-mismatch` result; the telemetry archive (`writeRollupShard`, `foldWithArchive`, `archiveShardPaths`); the install staging dir helpers; `validateInvariants`; `parseStatus`; `PROGRAM_GATEWAYS`; `HARVEST_TIMEOUT_MS`; `ADDITIVE_LABELS`; the `package.json` keys `bkit.renovateRunner` and `bkit.depUpdater: "renovate"`; tests that only asserted removed flags are rejected. Test helpers live in test files.
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: "do not keep unused features, remove all". Evidence per item: no importer outside its own test, no call site in workflows/prompts/CI/hooks, or no caller passing the option.

summary: bkit's own pnpm overrides and allowed build scripts live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
rationale: pnpm 11 ignores `pnpm.overrides` in `package.json` and blocks esbuild's build script unless allowed. Reason moved out of config comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own renovate.json5 holds vite and pnpm major updates
rationale: pnpm 11 ignores `pnpm.overrides` in `package.json` (they move to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) and blocks esbuild's build script unless it is listed in `onlyBuiltDependencies`, so a pnpm major would drop the vite pin. Reason moved out of the renovate.json5 comment (owner rule 2026-10-10).
description: `.github/renovate.json5` (bkit repo only) disables major updates for vite and pnpm; minor and patch stay enabled. vite stays on ^6 through `pnpm.overrides` in `package.json`.

summary: The `guardrails.cjs` hooks' empty catches are their fail-open contract
rationale: The empty catches implement the hook's fail-open contract: an internal error yields no decision. No further reason is written down. Reason moved out of the slop-scan config comment (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit carries no upgrade, migration or legacy-compat code
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: "we do NOT have to worry about existing users upgrading migrating - there are only two and we control both so any migration considerations are dead code as well". The two installs are this repo and consumer-a; old paths there are fixed by hand after a release.
description: Removed: retire lists (bkit-retire.ts), package.json repoint (bkit-package-json.ts), config.md to context.md migration (bkit-context-migrate.ts), telemetry migrate/validate/normalise, tier3Hashes fold, pre-envelope and envelope readers, hash-comment marker style, opencode provider aliases, status.json rewrite and fallback, legacy advisories.

summary: Agents never add migration code unasked; they suggest it and list manual fixes
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: a project rule not to add migration code unasked, only suggest. Shims added with each format change were never removed and accumulated (about 10,900 lines removed in #489).

summary: `bkit telemetry validate` and `normalise` are removed; `telemetry summary` stays
rationale: Both served the retired DE-N/KN-N key numbering. Run against consumer-a, validate reported issue-number prefixes in key names (KN-1210, KN-1219) as collisions.

summary: The version downgrade and stale-pin detectors read `pinnedVersion` from `.bkit/version`
rationale: They read the file as plain text, so they never fired on the JSON format every install writes.

summary: The `.npmrc` `_authToken` advisory (`npmrc-authtoken-line`) stays
rationale: Current hazard, not something an older bkit wrote: GitHub's docs tell people to write that line, and it causes 401s on pnpm >=10.34.3.

summary: One context list and one start-line parser serve the advisories and the `bkit context` runner
rationale: Two copies had drifted. The runner follows the advisories' stricter reading: a malformed start line opens no block.

summary: The template ci.yml ships the `bkit-tests-check` capstone, without a planner
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: ship the template with it switched on if required for bkit-ship to work. `runs gate`, `runs wait` and `setup protect-main` read only the capstone job and its result; no bkit command reads planner output. The executed-test count check applies only when the unit lane writes a count, which keeps the template stack-agnostic.

summary: Flags only tests passed are removed; tests set `package.json` `bkit.*` values instead
rationale: Follows 489-no-code-without-a-production-caller. Removed: `runs wait|gate --capstone/--ci-workflow/--required-lanes`, `--tracker` on `prs open` and `issues labels`, `runtime row --at`, `branches switch --lock-wait`, `--context-file`. The dev-lock wait has no setting, so its test mocks the timeouts module.

summary: `bkit comply` labels rows with `resolveRepoSlug`, like every other telemetry writer
rationale: `bkit.repoSlug` was a second source for the same value. No further reason is written down.

summary: The template-name table lives in `bkit-paths.ts`, so drift checks map `.gitignore` to the `gitignore` template
rationale: The `.gitignore` block was never drift-checked because the template file is named `gitignore`.

summary: The template path-reference test takes its names from every file `isTemplate` accepts
rationale: A hand-written list missed seven templates. `bkit-design-review-1` reading `docs/capabilities.md` "when present" is an allowed optional read, held as one narrow allowance.

summary: Workflows derive the auto-route suffix from `bkit issues labels` on the labels already read through MCP
rationale: The `gh issue view` reads broke the tracker-reads-through-MCP rule and failed silently on Linear or without `gh`. Linear issues now get the marker too.

summary: Workflows run `bkit comply` before `workflows close`
rationale: The close comment showed the previous run's compliance grade when comply ran after it.

summary: A required flag given an empty value exits 2 (USAGE)
rationale: An empty `--head=` from a failed probe went into the ship re-validate loop and a 170-minute mirror poll.

summary: `bkit branches rebase` aborts a refused rebase itself, before writing its log and sentinel
rationale: Leaving it in progress made the abort depend on the Failure Path running `workflows fail`. The abort resets tracked files, so it runs before the log and sentinel are written.

summary: The wording check splits sentences on `;`, requires `No commits` only in prompts that list `Bash`, and checks the whole header order
rationale: The `;` split and the Bash condition were agreed with the 2026-09-25 measurement and not built. The check missed a drifted fifth copy, a drifted Mandate line and swapped header lines.

summary: Ship's post-merge check passes or fails on the `bkit-tests-check` capstone job alone
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The capstone is the job branch protection requires and it decides what counts; other jobs (deploys, notifications) cannot fail the close of an already-merged PR.

summary: Design and plan worktrees install dependencies like build and debug
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Without an install there is no `.husky/_`, so commits and pushes in those worktrees skipped the hooks, and the design-spike subagent had no `node_modules`.

summary: Cleanup removes only marked worktrees; a branch held by an unmarked worktree keeps both its local and remote branch, and cleanup names the worktree
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The local delete failed silently while the remote branch was still deleted.

summary: A failed dependency install stops build, debug and ship
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Ship runs tests and the merge check; carrying on without dependencies only fails later with a less clear error.

summary: Branch sync merges ledger conflicts by union, aborts on a conflict outside `docs/`, and treats a failed fetch as fatal
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Ledgers are append-only, so union loses no rows where taking dev's side dropped the branch's rows; a code conflict needs a person or the conflict-resolve agent; syncing against a stale dev hides real conflicts.

summary: A stale lock is reclaimed as soon as its holder is idle; the lock file's age is not checked
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Reverts the 30-minute file-age condition. No further reason is written down.

summary: Every workflow runs the strict FID check at Step 1, with or without a tracker; `prs open` keeps its check as a backstop
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. A bad FID failed only at `prs open`, after the work was done; design with no tracker skipped the Step 1 check.

summary: `steps done` refuses a PASS with failures, a FAIL without, and missing or empty artifacts; debug diagnose requires `Mode:`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. A contradictory row means the subagent output is wrong; catching it at write time is cheaper than acting on a bad verdict later. Debug routes on `Mode:`.

summary: Ship's skill prune warns and carries on: a missing `.agents/skills.md` skips the prune, a failed uninstall is reported
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The PR has merged by then and pruning is housekeeping; a missing registry must never uninstall every skill.

summary: Design Step 3 skips a related issue whose comments don't parse and names it in the design inputs
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Related issues are background; one bad comment should not stop a design.

summary: The pre-worktree commit passes the repo root explicitly
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Without it the commit runs wherever the shell is, which can be a subfolder or another checkout.

summary: Status rows use `verdict` for complexity, `timeout_s` for ship, always write `attempt`, and record the PR URL in `artifacts`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Reverts the #467 renames (`complexity`, `timeoutS`, `attempt` omitted at 0, `prUrl`). No further reason is written down.

summary: `bkit steps gate` checks a row's `strategy`, `scope` and `attempt` wherever the step writes them
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The checklist lines were dropped while `steps done` still wrote the fields, so a row missing one passed its gate. The check lives in code, not in lines the agent ticks.

summary: Runtime detection has no `REPO_ROOT`/`FID` env fallback, and there is no `BKIT_MIRROR_GATE_SH` hook
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Workflows pass flags; the mirror-gate variable was test-only (489-no-code-without-a-production-caller).

summary: All 11 #467 section 4 centralisation items, the four outside-workflow items and the three excluded hook items are built, after #507's file move
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Items: steps finish, {BKIT} placeholder, land-on-dev helpers, workflows fail/handover, fids find/workflows promote, workflows close --outbox/links, labels into runs dispatch, ship-only helpers, auto runs context, steps gate in every gate, parseFlags placeholder guard; bkit ci prose, steps stub, one cloud context job, husky skip-CI regex from SKIP_CI_TOKEN; shared preflight.sh, slimmer cloud-bootstrap.sh, one gateguard/guardrails source. Done after the move so new commands land in their final folders.

summary: The wording check covers the workflows and the audit templates; per-family clauses and block-position checks are not built
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. 92 sentences repeat across the workflows and 83 across the audit templates with no check, and the workflow header lines had drifted.

summary: Auto's Timeouts line is 3600s, like the other workflows
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Auto hands off to a phase workflow that runs under 3600s; one value lets the line be one shared clause.

summary: Build commits its test-run log, clamped, under `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. In `.git/bkit-outbox` only, it was lost with the worktree.

summary: Uninstall deletes the owned `docs/templates/bkit-*.md` files and strips bkit's blocks from `docs/*.md`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Decision row 489-own-only-what-a-workflow-runs-four-file-groups wins over the code, which left `docs/` untouched.

summary: `bkit check` warns when a `bkit:gate:*` script is empty or a no-op (`true`, `:`, `exit 0`, `echo …`)
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Such a gate checks nothing, and only the gates audit caught it. Warn-only, so a deliberate stub does not block a push.

summary: The package splits `.bkit/templates/` into `.bkit/core/` (PolyForm, written and kept current), `.bkit/shared/` (MIT-0, written and kept current) and `.bkit/templates/` (MIT-0, copy-and-own); a file's path inside its folder is where it lands
rationale: Reverses the #489 decision of 2026-10-09 to copy only the template set and leave the package layout alone. That decision weighed the split against the cost of moving install paths and had no licence reason; #506 licenses bkit as PolyForm with low-IP files under MIT-0, and a licence must say which files are which without reading `isTemplate`.

summary: The engine lives at `.bkit/core/engine/`, split into `commands/` (what you type) and `install/`, `render/`, `checks/before/`, `checks/after/`, `ledgers/`, `shared/`, `tools/`; no `bkit-` prefix inside; tests sit next to the file they test, and tests that read shipped text sit in `audits/`
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10 approved the layout and file names posted on #507 (comment 6094807529), including its renames table. `engine/` not `src/` because every other path in `core/` is where install writes the file; `checks/before` and `checks/after` because detection runs before and after writing, and `preflight`/`postinstall` read as npm lifecycle hooks; `bin` points at `dist/cli.js`.

summary: No bkit release until #507's folder split lands; the pre-release check fails when `.bkit/templates/` holds anything but copy-and-own templates
rationale: `.bkit/templates/LICENSE.md` (MIT-0, c3fe30a8) covers that folder, which still holds `AGENTS.md`, the plan and audit templates and other core files until the split moves them; a release in between would put them under MIT-0.

summary: Every managed marker bkit writes names the PolyForm licence and its URL, and install writes `.bkit/LICENSE.md` with the full PolyForm text and its Required Notice
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10. PolyForm's Notices section requires anyone passing on a copy to pass on the terms (or their URL) and the Required Notice line; install copies PolyForm files (AGENTS.md, agents, commands, .bkit docs, hooks) into user repos that may be public, and core/LICENSE.md never went with them.

summary: `{BKIT}` is the bkit path `repo info` prints, held and filled in by the orchestrator; it is not an install-time token
rationale: No install or render change is needed, and the placeholder guard (a flag still holding `{UPPER}` exits 2) catches a missed substitution.

summary: Gate checks run inside `bkit steps finish`; `bkit steps gate` is called only where no finish runs (Step 1 gates, close gates, ship Steps 3 and 9, auto)
rationale: One code path checks a row's fields, right after it is written; a second call at every gate would repeat it.

summary: Ship keeps its 15 step names; Steps 3 and 9 write no row and check their values with `steps gate --placeholder`
rationale: The names are frozen by `ship-invariants.test.ts` and `checks/status-holes.ts`; new rows would break the status-hole check for every past ship.

summary: Ship's close and flush helpers live in `commands/workflow/workflows.ts`
rationale: Putting them in `branches.ts` makes `branches.ts` and `workflows.ts` import each other.

summary: `bkit workflows close` grades compliance before writing its report; workflows no longer call `bkit comply`
rationale: One writer, and the grade always lands in the close commit; before, the grade could be written after the commit.

summary: `bkit workflows fail` changes lock or label state only when given a lock token; an empty token counts as none
rationale: A failure before Step 1 takes the lock must not touch another run's lock.

summary: The Failure Path passes its error text to `workflows fail` / `issues comment` through `--error-file`, not a heredoc
rationale: Quotes or backticks in an error message broke the heredoc; a file carries any text unchanged.

summary: Every workflow re-asks the agent when its verdict header is PENDING (exit 5) or invalid (exit 6)
rationale: Build, debug and ship sent these to the Failure Path while design and plan re-asked; one rule, and a fixable agent slip no longer ends the run.

summary: The clamp-log helpers live in `ledgers/clamp-log.ts`
rationale: A file in `commands/workflow/` must be a command, and keeping the helpers out of `context.ts` broke an import cycle that crashed whenever `steps.ts` loaded first.

summary: Auto's CI mode reads the PR body through `gh`; there is no tracker MCP fallback
rationale: The CI-run lookup in the same step already needs `gh`; a second path for one field is not worth keeping.

summary: A step's allowed verdict values and header fields are declared once, in its prompt; workflow gates no longer repeat them
rationale: `steps finish` reads the prompt's declaration, so a value list in the workflow could only drift from it.

summary: The code all hosts' hooks share lives in `.bkit/core/hooks/` (moved there as `core/hook-parts/`, then renamed by #507), outside the templates folder
rationale: Under `.bkit/templates/` the install walk copied it to a `hook-parts/` folder at the root of the user's repo; it is bkit-written source spliced in at render time (`render/parts.ts`), not a template.

summary: Workflows run `bkit comply` before `workflows close`
description: Superseded by `467-compliance-graded-inside-workflows-close`: `bkit workflows close` grades compliance itself before writing its report, and no workflow calls `bkit comply`.
rationale: The close comment showed the grade of the previous run when comply ran after it.

summary: A file bkit stops shipping is deleted only when unchanged since bkit wrote it; an edited copy is kept with an advisory, callers are reported, and no shim is left at the old path
description: Superseded by `489-no-migration-code`: bkit carries no upgrade, migration or legacy-compat code. The retire engine (bkit-retire) was deleted in 8badea26; canonicalHashes now serve only the upgrade/uninstall drift checks, and a stale entry for an absent path is pruned by the install/upgrade merge (mergeCanonicalHashes).
rationale: Install and upgrade overwrite what bkit owns but never delete a file bkit has dropped, so a retired script would otherwise sit in every consumer repo forever; a consumer-edited copy stays; caller lines get their own advisory because nothing else tells the consumer the call now fails. Why no forwarding shim is left at a retired path is not written down.

summary: Auto's CI mode reads the PR body through `gh`; there is no tracker MCP fallback
rationale: The CI-run lookup in the same step already needs `gh`; a second path for one field is not worth keeping.

summary: Workflows derive the auto-route suffix from `bkit issues labels` on the labels already read through MCP
rationale: The `gh issue view` reads broke the tracker-reads-through-MCP rule and failed silently on Linear or without `gh`. Linear issues now get the marker too.

summary: Auto's Timeouts line is 3600s, like the other workflows
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Auto hands off to a phase workflow that runs under 3600s; one value lets the line be one shared clause.

summary: Workflow mechanics run as `bkit <noun> <verb>` commands under one contract: kebab-case flags, one JSON object on stdout, `[bkit-<noun>]` logs on stderr, fixed exit-code bands
description: Every mechanical workflow step is a `bkit <noun> <verb>` command in `.bkit/core/engine/commands/{workflow,ci,setup}/`, listed in `commands/registry.ts`; `conventions.test.ts` fails on an unlisted source file and holds every command to the contract in `commands/lib.ts`. Flags: kebab-case, `--flag=value` or `--flag value`, one name for one thing everywhere (`--workflow --step --fid --month --sub-plan --attempt --verdict --artifact`). stdout: ONE JSON object, camelCase keys matching `status.jsonl`. stderr: human log lines tagged `[bkit-<noun>]`. Exit: 0 ok / 1 the answer is no (gate failed, max attempts, lock held) / 2 usage error or missing dependency; 3-79 command-specific, listed in that verb's `--help`; 80 do it via MCP (`gh` unavailable); 81 hand the wait back to the agent turn loop; 82 needs a human. `--help` renders from the verb's own spec. Nouns are plural where a repo has many (`counters`), singular where it has one (`status`). `bkit <noun> <verb>` is tried before the older top-level commands; a noun that is also a command (`status`) routes only when the second word is one of its verbs. Workflow blocks call the main checkout's binary through the fixed `BKIT=` line; the bkit repo links itself as a dev dependency for the same path. A value a later step needs is held from the JSON by key, never re-derived; `jq` in a workflow block only picks one key out of a command's output in that block. The slop plugin `bkit-slop-type-suppression.mjs` is a template at `.bkit/templates/scripts/slop/`, not a script a workflow runs.
rationale: Stated in the #467 commits and code: the contract is fixed once in `commands/lib.ts` so flag names, output shape and exit codes are not copied per command (8d3c3dcf); `--help` and the convention test read the same spec, so help text cannot drift from what a command accepts (`commands/lib.ts` header). Repo facts each workflow worked out by hand — repo root from any worktree, UTC month, where `status.jsonl` lives, skip-CI tokens — now have one answer (8d3c3dcf); porting surfaced hand-derived bugs, e.g. macOS reading UTC timestamps as local time, which made a live run look ten hours idle and lose its lock (8dc60537). Logic lives in commands, not workflow shell, because the host shell is not guaranteed bash and a workflow body cannot take shell positional parameters — slash-command argument substitution rewrites `$N` (`.agents/rules.md` § Project Rules › Workflow bash blocks; `.bkit/workflows.md` § Workflow Authoring Rules) — and because a workflow that runs an installed script by path breaks when the consumer renames or deletes it (`.bkit/core/engine/audits/templates/template-path-refs.test.ts`). The main-checkout binary works before and without a worktree `node_modules`, since design and plan worktrees never install (`.bkit/workflows.md` § Workflow commands).
alternatives: Shell scripts that workflows source or run — rejected for the reasons in the rationale. Not written down anywhere: why one JSON object rather than shell `KEY=value` lines, and why exit codes 80-82 specifically.

summary: Branch sync merges ledger conflicts by union, aborts on a conflict outside `docs/`, and treats a failed fetch as fatal
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Ledgers are append-only, so union loses no rows where taking dev's side dropped the branch's rows; a code conflict needs a person or the conflict-resolve agent; syncing against a stale dev hides real conflicts.

summary: Build commits its test-run log, clamped, under `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. In `.git/bkit-outbox` only, it was lost with the worktree.

summary: Cleanup removes only marked worktrees; a branch held by an unmarked worktree keeps both its local and remote branch, and cleanup names the worktree
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The local delete failed silently while the remote branch was still deleted.

summary: Design and plan worktrees install dependencies like build and debug
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Without an install there is no `.husky/_`, so commits and pushes in those worktrees skipped the hooks, and the design-spike subagent had no `node_modules`.

summary: Design Step 3 skips a related issue whose comments don't parse and names it in the design inputs
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Related issues are background; one bad comment should not stop a design.

summary: A required flag given an empty value exits 2 (USAGE)
rationale: An empty `--head=` from a failed probe went into the ship re-validate loop and a 170-minute mirror poll.

summary: Every workflow runs the strict FID check at Step 1, with or without a tracker; `prs open` keeps its check as a backstop
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. A bad FID failed only at `prs open`, after the work was done; design with no tracker skipped the Step 1 check.

summary: A failed dependency install stops build, debug and ship
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Ship runs tests and the merge check; carrying on without dependencies only fails later with a less clear error.

summary: Workflows write `status.jsonl` and `.bkit/issues.jsonl` rows only through `bkit` commands; no workflow block appends with `>>`
description: Row writers: `workflow-started` / `workflow-failed` / `workflow-done` plus close telemetry → `bkit workflows start|fail|close`; `step-done` → `bkit steps done` (captures `parentSha`, writes the row, then commits, in that order); `workflow-meta` → `bkit status meta` (`--debug-mode` / `--push-mode` / `--debug-attempt` / `--plan-source` / `--soak-entry` / `--opened-pr`); `runtime-resolved` → `bkit runtime row`; `transport-fallback` / `close-transport` → `bkit prs transport-row`; any other typed audit row the fold does not model (ship's gate refusals, CI probes, timeouts, merge CI) → `bkit status row --type=`, which refuses a folded type; `kind:"feature"` rows → `bkit roadmap feature` (appends, re-renders `docs/roadmap.md`, fail-open). Reads go through `bkit status fold|route` and `bkit counters derive|rows|run`; no counter is derived by raw jq over `status.jsonl`. `bkit workflows close` runs in the worktree before the squash in both close modes, so its rows ride the branch. Gates: `ship-invariants.test.ts` (no `>>` onto `status.jsonl` or `.bkit/issues.jsonl` in any phase workflow) and `counter-prose-audit.test.ts` (no raw-jq counter).
rationale: A raw `>>` bypasses the row shape and the fail-open contract the commands own (`ship-invariants.test.ts`). `bkit steps gate` checks the row `steps done` wrote, so a step no longer types its own row and then ticks a box saying it did; `steps done` orders parentSha capture, row and commit because the fold's de-dup key needs `parentSha` to advance per attempt (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/steps.ts` header). Close rows written in the worktree before the squash ride the branch (045e990f).
alternatives: No rejected alternative is recorded in the #467 commits, `.bkit/workflows.md` or `docs/architecture.md`.

summary: The pre-worktree commit passes the repo root explicitly
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Without it the commit runs wherever the shell is, which can be a subfolder or another checkout.

summary: `bkit branches rebase` aborts a refused rebase itself, before writing its log and sentinel
rationale: Leaving it in progress made the abort depend on the Failure Path running `workflows fail`. The abort resets tracked files, so it runs before the log and sentinel are written.

summary: Runtime detection has no `REPO_ROOT`/`FID` env fallback, and there is no `BKIT_MIRROR_GATE_SH` hook
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Workflows pass flags; the mirror-gate variable was test-only (489-no-code-without-a-production-caller).

summary: Ship's post-merge check passes or fails on the `bkit-tests-check` capstone job alone
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The capstone is the job branch protection requires and it decides what counts; other jobs (deploys, notifications) cannot fail the close of an already-merged PR.

summary: Ship's skill prune warns and carries on: a missing `.agents/skills.md` skips the prune, a failed uninstall is reported
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The PR has merged by then and pruning is housekeeping; a missing registry must never uninstall every skill.

summary: Ship keeps its 15 step names; Steps 3 and 9 write no row and check their values with `steps gate --placeholder`
rationale: The names are frozen by `ship-invariants.test.ts` and `checks/status-holes.ts`; new rows would break the status-hole check for every past ship.

summary: A stale lock is reclaimed as soon as its holder is idle; the lock file's age is not checked
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Reverts the 30-minute file-age condition. No further reason is written down.

summary: Status rows use `verdict` for complexity, `timeout_s` for ship, always write `attempt`, and record the PR URL in `artifacts`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Reverts the #467 renames (`complexity`, `timeoutS`, `attempt` omitted at 0, `prUrl`). No further reason is written down.

summary: `steps done` refuses a PASS with failures, a FAIL without, and missing or empty artifacts; debug diagnose requires `Mode:`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. A contradictory row means the subagent output is wrong; catching it at write time is cheaper than acting on a bad verdict later. Debug routes on `Mode:`.

summary: `bkit steps gate` checks a row's `strategy`, `scope` and `attempt` wherever the step writes them
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The checklist lines were dropped while `steps done` still wrote the fields, so a row missing one passed its gate. The check lives in code, not in lines the agent ticks.

summary: A step's allowed verdict values and header fields are declared once, in its prompt; workflow gates no longer repeat them
rationale: `steps finish` reads the prompt's declaration, so a value list in the workflow could only drift from it.

summary: The wording check covers the workflows and the audit templates; per-family clauses and block-position checks are not built
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. 92 sentences repeat across the workflows and 83 across the audit templates with no check, and the workflow header lines had drifted.

summary: Sentences shared by 5+ prompts, and header sentences workflows share with prompts, live once in `.bkit/wording.md`; a test checks every copy and `pnpm wording:sync` rewrites them in place
description: `.bkit/wording.md` holds one clause per shared sentence: canonical `text`, earlier wordings in `retired`, and a mode per surface (`required` / `where-used` / `forbidden` / `if-verdict`) for prompts, workflows and the `.agents/rules.md` managed block. `.bkit/core/engine/tools/wording.test.ts` fails on a missing, duplicated or forbidden clause, a near-copy (80%+ similar, not equal), a retired wording, and any sentence in 5+ prompts the file does not list; it also keeps the Rules line first, External input last, the `.agents/rules.md` group headings, and the three legs of the untrusted-input sentence. `pnpm wording:sync` (`.bkit/core/engine/tools/wording.ts --write`) rewrites near-copies and retired wordings in place, finding copies by similarity and each clause's retired list, so prompts carry no markers. Change a shared sentence only in `.bkit/wording.md`: edit `text`, move the old wording to `retired`, run `pnpm wording:sync`. Sentences in fewer than 5 prompts stay local.
rationale: Changing a shared sentence becomes one edit plus one command instead of up to 48 hand edits (81878ecf). The check found real drift on its first run: the Destructive git line in `bkit-ship-conflict-resolve`, and a comma for a semicolon in the Tools line of six workflows (81878ecf).
alternatives: Markers in each prompt around the shared text — not used: sync finds copies by similarity and retired wordings so no markers are added (81878ecf); why markers were unwanted is not written down. Render-time assembly of prompt headers at `bkit install` — listed as deferred in `de-36-342-universal-untrusted-input-bullet-plus-glob-scoped-g`; #467 records no reason for choosing in-place sync over it.

summary: The wording check splits sentences on `;`, requires `No commits` only in prompts that list `Bash`, and checks the whole header order
rationale: The `;` split and the Bash condition were agreed with the 2026-09-25 measurement and not built. The check missed a drifted fifth copy, a drifted Mandate line and swapped header lines.

summary: No workflow, prompt or `.bkit/wording.md` names an installed template path; mechanics come from `bkit` commands and settings from `package.json` `bkit`
description: `.bkit/core/engine/audits/templates/template-path-refs.test.ts` fails when a line in `.bkit/core/workflows/*.md`, `.bkit/core/prompts/*.md` or `.bkit/wording.md` names a template path: each `.github/workflows/` template file name, `.husky/`, `.vale`, `.lintstagedrc.json`, `slop-scan.config.json`, `.envrc`, and each `scripts/<tool>/` template folder. The workflow and script names are read from `.bkit/templates/`, so a new template is covered without editing the test. Settings a command needs come from `package.json` `bkit` through one reader, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/shared/config.ts`: `ciWorkflow` (default `ci.yml`), `capstoneJob` (default `bkit-tests-check`), `worktree.copy` (default `.env`, `.env.local`), `worktree.install` (default true), `issueTracker`, `githubProject`, `shipGateRequiredLanes` (default empty). No command hard-codes a CI workflow, check name or app folder.
rationale: Templates are the consumer's once installed: they rename, delete or rewrite them (a CI workflow, a hook, a lint config, a helper script), and a workflow step that reads or runs one by path breaks the day the consumer does (`.bkit/core/engine/audits/templates/template-path-refs.test.ts` header). One settings reader gives one set of defaults (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/shared/config.ts` header).
alternatives: A hand-maintained forbidden-path list in the test — not used: names derive from the templates folder so a new template is covered without editing the test (test header). No other alternative is recorded.

summary: Capitals mark only a hard limit; closed list NEVER, ALWAYS, MUST, ONLY, PROHIBITED
description: Notation rule (`.bkit/prompts.md` § Notation; binds prompts, workflows, `.agents/rules.md` and docs): a word takes capitals only when it marks a hard limit — a destructive, irreversible or security-sensitive action, or a required field / machine-parsed invariant. Closed list `NEVER`, `ALWAYS`, `MUST`, `ONLY`, `PROHIBITED`; everything else lowercase, scope quantifiers and joining words included. One capitalised word per clause; never inside a label, a parenthetical or a description.
rationale: OpenAI GPT-5.6 reserves ALWAYS / NEVER / must / only for true invariants; Anthropic says dial back aggressive wording on current models; no prompt guide read supports capitals on judgement calls. The 2026-10 prompt audit (prompts-3, HIGH) found ~60% of bkit provider of 1,021 capitalised prompt words on process / judgement lines, and the style predates every current model pin.
alternatives: Capitalise scope quantifiers (ALL / ANY / EVERY) as invariants — rejected: they mark scope, not safety or a required field, and no guide supports them. Keep the mixed-case NOT contrast marker — rejected: emphasis without a tier.

summary: NEVER = forbidden everywhere; do not = forbidden in this step; mixed-case do NOT retired
description: Two distinct forms replace the interchangeable `NEVER` / `do NOT` mix. `NEVER` marks a hard limit forbidden everywhere, at all times; lowercase `do not` marks a prohibition scoped to the step. `do NOT` is retired — it added emphasis without marking a tier.
rationale: No prompt guide read distinguishes `NEVER` from `do NOT`; OpenAI groups `NEVER` with the invariant markers, Anthropic prefers the positive form. The audit counted 393 `do NOT` and 183 `NEVER` across the prompts, 16 lines carrying both, with no recorded difference.
alternatives: Drop `NEVER` for `do not` everywhere — rejected: a hard limit forbidden at all times is worth marking distinctly, and OpenAI guide backs it.

summary: One short reason clause allowed on a hard limit a model would otherwise misread
description: `.bkit/prompts.md` § Prompt Authoring Rules § Dense instructions only keeps no-rationale as the default and carves one exception: a single short reason clause on a hard limit whose boundary a model would otherwise misread or over-apply. The exception reaches prompts and workflows through § Notation.
rationale: Anthropic guide asks for the reason behind an instruction and no prompt guide read forbids it; the blanket ban departed from it. A one-clause reason costs ~5-15 tokens and only where the boundary is non-obvious. bkit-ship-conflict-resolve already carried the one recorded example.
alternatives: Keep the blanket ban — rejected: no guide read supports it and Anthropic asks for the reason. Allow a reason on every rule — rejected: every byte is paid on every run.

summary: Capitals mark only a hard limit; closed list NEVER, ALWAYS, MUST, ONLY, PROHIBITED
description: Notation rule (`.bkit/prompts.md` § Notation; binds prompts, workflows, `.agents/rules.md` and docs): a word takes capitals only when it marks a hard limit — a destructive, irreversible or security-sensitive action, or a required field / machine-parsed invariant. Closed list `NEVER`, `ALWAYS`, `MUST`, `ONLY`, `PROHIBITED`; everything else lowercase, scope quantifiers and joining words included. One capitalised word per clause; never inside a label, a parenthetical or a description.
rationale: OpenAI GPT-5.6 reserves ALWAYS / NEVER / must / only for true invariants; Anthropic says dial back aggressive wording on current models; no prompt guide read supports capitals on judgement calls. The 2026-10 prompt audit (prompts-3, HIGH) found ~60% of bkit 1,021 capitalised prompt words on process / judgement lines, and the style predates every current model pin.
alternatives: Capitalise scope quantifiers (ALL / ANY / EVERY) as invariants — rejected: they mark scope, not safety or a required field, and no guide supports them. Keep the mixed-case NOT contrast marker — rejected: emphasis without a tier.

summary: Summary output cap applies to prose only; sections listing items verbatim are exempt
description: Shared `output-cap` wording clause (`.bkit/wording.md` § output-cap; reaches the four summary prompts and bkit-debug-abort-handover): apply max 500 token limit to **Create** prose; sections that list items verbatim are exempt. Cap-table row in `.bkit/prompts.md` restated to match.
rationale: The 2026-10 prompt audit (prompts-5) found the blanket 500-token cap always lost to the verbatim-list clause — 35 of 36 sampled summary outputs over cap, median 1,686 words. The cap exists for Linear comment readability; the verbatim lists are the human's decision surface where rewording loses the trade-off. Scoping preserves both instead of sacrificing either.
alternatives: Drop the cap — rejected: loses the Linear UX guard the cap exists for. Cut the verbatim requirement — rejected: a reworded acceptance item or option loses the trade-off the human decides on. Raise the cap — rejected: no data picks a new number.

summary: Plan split decision keys on task count (<= 12); unestimable 85K token figure dropped
description: `bkit-plan-complexity-check` verdict maps `SINGLE` = task count <= 12, `SPLIT` = task count > 12; `bkit-plan-complexity-split` sizes sub-plans at <= 12 tasks (ceil(tasks / 12) sub-plans). The 85K estimated-token threshold and the estimation step removed from both prompts.
rationale: The 2026-10 prompt audit (prompts-11) found the split decision rested on an estimated-token figure with no estimation method — a number no agent can derive. Task count is countable by grep, was already the secondary anchor, and gates / domain areas remain counted as advisory context. Adding invented gate or domain thresholds would repeat the same ungrounded-number problem.
alternatives: Define a token-estimation method — rejected: any per-task token constant would be as ungrounded as 85K. Add gate / domain thresholds — rejected: no data picks the numbers.

summary: No CI gate on open CRITICAL failures and no automated stale-deferral report; the failures and deferrals audits cover both on cadence
description: #346 proposed gating CI on open CRITICAL failures and reporting stale OPEN deferrals. Decision: not built. docs/templates/bkit-audit-failures.md and docs/templates/bkit-audit-deferrals.md already encode the required semantics (open = status != CLOSED incl. TRIAGED; age from the earliest row per key; case-insensitive severity; ts/status data-defect checks) on a per-cycle / monthly cadence, with an extra pass on new CRITICAL rows. The failures audit gate question (bkit-audit-failures.md:52, :106) recording the gate as absent is the decided state, not a gap. Two incidental fixes stay open: ledger-integrity.test.ts validates envelope/kind/reason/future-ts but not severity, status or ts:0 (bad rows: failure severity "low" duplicated; deferral 384-mode-3-bookkeeping-e2e-deferred-to-341-live-run ts:0); .bkit/jsonl.md:145 (CRITICAL triage before next release) contradicts :254 (TRIAGED is STILL open WORK).
rationale: The proposal risk (open CRITICALs invisible, stale deferrals forgotten) is already mitigated by the audit cadence that landed after #80 closed; a second continuous mechanism duplicates it and would contradict the schema (jsonl.md:145 vs :254). 0 open CRITICAL failures and 68 open deferrals (none HIGH or CRITICAL) mean a gate would never fire today.
alternatives: Build the gate inside bkit check, failing on release only (release.yml would need a new step) - rejected (owner, 2026-10-11): the audits are enough.

summary: plan grounded on the canonical design despite no Parent design marker
description: Issue #504 carried no **Parent design:** marker, so /bkit-plan Step 1 would default PARENT_FID empty (standalone plan). The canonical design docs/plans/202610/504-example-project-design.md exists for the same FID and month and the issue is design-driven, so it was treated as the parent design and appended to plan-input-1.md.
rationale: A plan cannot be generated faithfully without its design; producing a standalone plan over an existing canonical design would be an incomplete shortcut.
alternatives: literal standalone plan on issue input alone (PARENT_FID empty)

summary: Shortcuts ship as inspiration-style copy-paste prompts, not commands
description: Issue #541 asked for quick-fix prompts outside the 5-phase pipeline. Shipped .agents/shortcuts.md as a managed doctrine doc (block-merged; consumer Project Shortcuts below bkit:end). One parameterized paste prompt points the agent at .bkit/workflows.md section Per-Phase Workflows and .bkit/prompts.md as inspiration only: take the steps and subagents that fit, drop the rest. Its Contract keeps rules, tracker In progress to In review, commit-as-you-go, no push. When NOT plus hard limits escalate schema / API / deps / secrets / auth / multi-file work to the real phase. bkit-utility-update-roadmap Step 11 recommends the shortcut prompt for a small, understood item.
rationale: The 5 phases are heavy by design; a one-concern change with a known approach either ran the whole phase or lost tracker discipline and subagent review. Pointing at the existing workflow as inspiration keeps the real workflow the single source of truth, so the shortcuts never drift and need no parallel lite procedure to maintain.
alternatives: Rigid per-phase lite flows with fixed subagent chains - rejected (drift and maintenance, duplicates the workflows). Real /bkit-quick-* commands rendered to every host - rejected (heaviest surface for a read-only prompt). Point at the rendered command files .claude/commands/bkit-*.md instead of the reference doc - rejected: they carry a No Improv Execution Protocol (no skipping, no alternative approaches) that contradicts inspiration.

summary: OpenCode network allows stay unanchored *{base}* globs, covering apex and every subdomain; the URL-smuggling match is an accepted risk
description: OpenCode matches permission keys as anchored globs over the whole URL or command (* becomes .*, crossing / ? @ #). Derived keys are *{base}* in permission.webfetch and curl|wget *{base}* in permission.bash, for each allowlist base. These match the base anywhere in the URL, so https://evil.tld/?x=github.com and https://github.com.evil.tld/ are allowed without a prompt. A host-anchored https://{host}/* shape closes that, but no OpenCode glob can express 'any subdomain' safely (https://*.{base}/* matches https://evil.tld/?a=.{base}/), so it drops subdomain coverage and every subdomain fetch prompts. Maintainer accepted the smuggling risk to keep apex + subdomain parity with Claude's WebFetch(domain:{base}) + WebFetch(domain:*.{base}). Claude Code's domain: rule checks the real hostname and is not affected.
rationale: A glob cannot express a single DNS label, so any subdomain wildcard lets a prompt-injected agent fetch attacker URLs without a prompt. Prompting on an unlisted subdomain is the safe failure.
alternatives: https://*.{base}/* - rejected (matches https://evil.tld/?a=.github.com/). *{base}* - rejected (substring match anywhere in the URL).

references: docs/deployments.md § Renovate pnpm-11 freshness gate & microvm memory
summary: The Renovate example caps pnpm's worker pool in Renovate's runner and enforces release age in Renovate, with pnpm's own `minimumReleaseAge` set to 0
description: `env: { PNPM_WORKERS: "1", PNPM_MAX_WORKERS: "1" }` and `minimumReleaseAge: "7 days"` in `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`; consumers set `minimumReleaseAge: 0` in pnpm-workspace.yaml.
rationale: On a large pnpm-11 monorepo, `pnpm update --lockfile-only`, especially alongside a pnpm-level `minimumReleaseAge` gate that verifies publish timestamps for every lockfile entry, can exceed the physical memory of Mend's hosted microvm and fail with `kernel-out-of-memory` (a physical OOM, not a V8 heap limit), blocking every dependency PR; CI and Vercel pass because their runners have far more RAM (KN-CORE-10, KN-41). The worker cap is cheap and reversible and scoped to Renovate's runner, but may not clear a metadata-driven OOM on its own because `--lockfile-only` barely engages the worker pool. Enforcing release age in Renovate holds young dependencies out of PRs with no per-install timestamp check, removing the memory spike at the source and speeding every CI and Vercel build; security and OSV PRs bypass it, so CVE fixes are never delayed. pnpm 11 defaults the gate to 1440, so deleting the key leaves it active and drops the `@cbartens/*` exclusion, breaking same-day bkit upgrades; only 0 turns the per-entry check off. The trade-off is losing pnpm-level defence against fresh manual or transitive installs. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

references: docs/deployments.md § Renovate pnpm-11 freshness gate & microvm memory
summary: The Renovate example caps pnpm's worker pool in Renovate's runner and enforces release age in Renovate, with pnpm's own `minimumReleaseAge` set to 0
description: `env: { PNPM_WORKERS: "1", PNPM_MAX_WORKERS: "1" }` and `minimumReleaseAge: "7 days"` in `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`; consumers set `minimumReleaseAge: 0` in pnpm-workspace.yaml.

The worker cap is cheap and reversible and scoped to Renovate's runner, but may not clear a metadata-driven OOM on its own because `--lockfile-only` barely engages the worker pool. Enforcing release age in Renovate holds young dependencies out of PRs with no per-install timestamp check, removing the memory spike at the source and speeding every CI and Vercel build; security and OSV PRs bypass it, so CVE fixes are never delayed. pnpm 11 defaults the gate to 1440, so deleting the key leaves it active and drops the `@cbartens/*` exclusion, breaking same-day bkit upgrades; only 0 turns the per-entry check off.
